title: Banking Center Manager, Canton, CT
description:
Banking Center Manager, Canton, CT

Country: United States of America

It Starts With You:

Santander is a global leader and innovator in the financial services industry and is evolving from a high-impact brand into a technology-driven organization. Our people are at the heart of this journey and together, we are driving a customer-centric transformation that values bold thinking, innovation, and the courage to challenge what’s possible. This is more than a strategic shift. It’s a chance for driven professionals to grow, learn, and make a real difference.


If you are interested in exploring the possibilities We Want to Talk to You!

The Difference You Make:

Webster Bank, a division of Santander Bank, N.A.

This role is responsible for all functions, staff, and daily operations within a banking center. They are responsible for implementing the banking center network strategy, which includes achievement of sales, customer service, P&L management, operations, and colleague development goals while also contributing to the achievement of District goals. This role is tasked with acquisition, integration, and optimization of new and existing client relationships. The colleague must develop and maintain a strong level of partnership with segment and line of business partners through collaboration and communication.

  • Consistently meet/exceed all sales goals, retention goals, and Superior Service Quality (SSQ) standards.
  • Develop, implement, and manage a detailed business plan and participate in establishing team sales and service goals.
  • Expand and retain client relationships, actively cross-sell and resolve client issues. Support segmentation strategy with existing clients by implementing sales, retention and other bank initiatives to support Banking Center’s growth and profitability objectives.
  • Identify, cultivate, and support key customer segment relationships through focused sales and referral activity.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of all asset, liability, and partner products and services as well as alternative delivery channels.
  • Coach, develop and hold team accountable by demonstrating leadership skills and modeling the way.
  • Utilize and model usage of all available sales tools and resources.
  • Ensure timely completion of audits with an expectation to meet/ exceed branch operations review requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with Federal and State laws as well as bank policies and procedures.
  • Schedule all branch employee shifts to meet customer service needs; provides flexibility of coverage for the banking center.
  • Drive high performance by holding team accountable for superior results. Enhance employee engagement by providing team with coaching, support, timely and constructive performance feedback. Provide opportunity in career growth and recognize and reward employees for accomplishments.
  • Execute on effective colleague onboarding, training new colleagues on policies, procedures and all banking center operational duties/responsibilities.

What You Bring:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Education:
  • H.S. Diploma or General Education Degree (GED) required
  • Advanced degrees (Associates and/or Bachelor's)

Qualifications:
  • 5-7 years of banking experience, with a proven track record in leadership, customer service, managerial, communication and organization skills required
  • Intricate knowledge of retail banking products and services.
  • Strong customer service skills, relationship building, organizational, computer skills, comfortable with current technology, and communication skills.

Certifications:

  • No Certifications listed for this job.

It Would Be Nice For You To Have:

  • Established work history or equivalent demonstrated through a combination of work experience, training, military service, or education.

Work Authorization & Sponsorship:
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without requiring employer sponsorship to commence employment.

What Else You Need To Know:

The base pay range for this position is posted below and represents the annualized salary range. For hourly positions (non-exempt), the annual range is based on a 40-hour work week. The exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, training, licensure and certifications and location.

Base Pay Range:

Minimum:

$60,000.00 USD

Maximum:

$102,500.00 USD

We Value Your Impact:

Your contribution matters and it’s recognized. You can expect a fair and competitive rewards package that reflects the impact you create and the value you deliver. We know rewards go beyond numbers. Offering more than just a paycheck our benefits are designed to support you, your family and your well-being, now and into the future. Santander Benefits - 2026 Santander OnGoing/NH eGuide (foleon.com)

Risk Culture:

We embrace a strong risk culture and all of our professionals at all levels are expected to take a proactive and responsible approach toward risk management.

EEO Statement:

At Santander, we value and respect differences in our workforce. We actively encourage everyone to apply. Santander is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law.

Working Conditions:

Frequent minimal physical effort such as sitting, standing and walking is required for this role. Depending on location, occasional moving and lifting light equipment and/or furniture may be required.

Employer Rights:

This job description does not list all of the job duties of the job. You may be asked by your supervisors or managers to perform other duties. You may be evaluated in part based upon your performance of the tasks listed in this job description. The employer has the right to revise this job description at any time. This job description is not a contract for employment and either you or the employer may terminate your employment at any time for any reason.

What To Do Next:

If this sounds like a role you are interested in, then please apply.

We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible application process for all candidates. If you require any assistance or accommodation due to a disability or any other reason, please contact us at TAOps@santander.us to discuss your needs.

title: Business Intelligence Developer II
description:

Department

Job Description


This position is Hybrid and will require 1 day on site at Winchester Medical Center per week (can vary based on projects/implementations).



Job Description

The Business Intelligence Developer II is responsible for analytic solutions development to support insights and effective decision making within Valley Health System (VHS).


Responsibilities and Duties

  • Create new analytical content, enhances existing analytics, and develops improvement efforts to the VHS analytics ecosystem.
  • Partners and coordinates with customers, informatics, and applications to ensure the appropriateness and accuracy of data and analytic solutions within VHS analytic ecosystem
  • Partners with the broader analytics team to support data lineage, security, effective data strategy, and user confidence in the validity, integrity, and action ability of the VHS data and analytic solutions.
  • Curates analytic content through the development lifecycle, requiring understanding, development, testing, validating, training, and deployment.
  • Confirms that new analytics adhere to data and platform standards created in partnership with data architects, data governance, data engineering, and other relevant teams
  • Acts as a subject matter resource for business intelligence solution development and if appropriate, inclusive of Epic’s enterprise intelligence and analytics suite.
  • Adheres, contributes to and supports data and analytic standards and processes.
  • Drives program outcomes, self-manages interdependencies between projects, project teams, and technical resources across multiple functions
  • Works on medium to large requests and initiatives. Focuses is on analytic program components execution and learning planning aspects
  • Works with moderate supervision, escalates higher-level issues but handles most operational decisions
  • Regularly interacts with cross-functional stakeholders and responsible for reporting on program status and issues
  • Secondary responsibilities as assigned within analytic services.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field or equivalent work experience is required.


Experience

  • 3+ years of experience creating and deploying analytics using Business Intelligence tools, including data visualization, developing reports/dashboards, and self-service data tools is required.
  • 3+ years of experience writing business logic in SQL or other similar coding language is required.
  • 3+ Experience and credibility interacting with analytics, technology, and healthcare leadership is required.
  • 3+ years of experience building dynamic analytical capabilities inclusive of reporting, dashboards, extracts, BI tools, analytical web applications and other similar products is required.
  • 3+ years of experience with Epic Cogito Analytics tool stack and/or certification is required.
  • 1+ years of experience with health system operations, business, and clinical ecosystems are required.

Qualifications

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and teamwork skills for working with cross-functional teams.



Benefits

At Valley Health, we believe everyone is a caregiver, and our goal is to create an environment where our caregivers thrive physically, financially, and emotionally. In addition to a competitive salary, our most popular benefits for full-time employees include:

  • A Zero-Deductible Health Plan
  • Dental and vision insurance
  • Generous Paid Time Off
  • Tuition Assistance
  • Retirement Savings Match
  • A Robust Employee Assistance Program to help with many aspects of emotional wellbeing
  • Membership to Healthy U: An Incentive-Based Wellness Program

Valley Health also offers a health savings account & flexible spending account for childcare, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability, and professional development. In addition, several perks come with working for the largest employer in the region, such as discounts to on-campus dining, and more.

title: Digital Seller
description:
At Dow, we believe in putting people first and we’re passionate about delivering integrity, respect and safety to our customers, our employees and the planet.

Our people are at the heart of our solutions. They reflect the communities we live in and the world where we do business. Their diversity is our strength. We’re a community of relentless problem solvers that offers the daily opportunity to contribute with your perspective, transform industries and shape the future. Our purpose is simple - to deliver a sustainable future for the world through science and collaboration. If you’re looking for a challenge and meaningful role, you’re in the right place.

Responsible for growing and nurturing customer relationships by selling new and existing product, as well as generating new customers, through a fully digitalized customer experience. Accountable for processes and tasks inherent in the sales process, including actioning leads and onboarding new customers, educating and positioning customers to partner with Dow through digital channels, and leveraging industry & product knowledge to drive sales. This position typically handles a small to medium sized customer portfolio consisting of foundational customers, while prospecting new ones. Scope typically includes accounts in a single country or across a limited number of countries and can be market segment specific or cross market segments. The role works under the guidance of a Sales Leader and in close collaboration with other experienced team members in Sales and Marketing. It can be an entry level position for university graduates with no to little job-related experience.


Responsibilities and Tasks

  • Develop customer pipeline, adding new foundational customers and developing existing customers to ‘Target Growth’.
    • Build strong customer relationships through digital channels and virtual partnership
    • Act as Dow.com ambassador and drive adoption of the platform with customers. Initial Dow.com account set-up for newly onboarded customers
    • Lead price/volume negotiations with customers; engage internal partners as needed
    • Maintain and update all pricing in Smartprice
    • Communicate product availability and lead times; troubleshoot availability challenges
    • Guide customers regarding options within the defined Service Offering Framework
    • Gather high-level market intelligence and customer insights; share within Dow
  • Lead & Opportunity Management
    • Generate, triage, route and develop leads and close opportunities in line with L&OM guidelines
    • Maintain and update CRM and internal tools
  • Digital Tools & Platforms
    • Obtain and maintain customer forecasts in OMP
    • Monitor sales vs. Forecast/plan through digital tools and take action accordingly
    • Communicate changes in sales forecasts to Product Management and Supply Chain
    • Be an early adopter of new technology, support testing for optimizing commercial tools
    • Participate in Sales, Product/Marketing strategy calls to obtain business and pricing guidelines
  • Participate in annual review of Channel purchasing strategy (direct/distribution) and segmentation
  • Support Order to Cash process to ensure correct invoicing and timely payment collection

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Solid negotiation and sales tactics
  • General understanding of products and product application rules
  • Understanding of business and financial interdependencies (cost, freight, margin, etc.)
  • Proactive hunter with ‘owner’s mindset’ & cold calling skills; self-driven and efficient
  • Technologically savvy & data driven, early adopter of new technology
  • Proficiency in CRM, DSR, SmartPrice, Dow.com, Microsoft Office

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree, fluency in English (verbally and in writing)


Benefits – What Dow offers you

We invest in you.

Dow invests in total rewards programs to help you manage all aspects of you: your pay, your health, your life, your future, and your career. You bring your background, talent, and perspective to work every day. Dow rewards that commitment by investing in your total wellbeing.

Here are just a few highlights of what you would be offered as a Dow employee:

  • Equitable and market-competitive base pay and bonus opportunity across our global markets, along with locally relevant incentives.
  • Benefits and programs to support your physical, mental, financial, and social well-being, to help you get the care you need...when you need it.
  • Competitive retirement program that may include company-provided benefits, savings opportunities, financial planning, and educational resources to help you achieve your long term financial-goals.
    • Employee stock purchase programs (availability varies depending on location).
  • Student Debt Retirement Savings Match Program (U.S. only).
    • Dow will take the value of monthly student debt payments and apply them as if they are contributions to the Employees’ Savings Plan (401(k)), helping employees reach the Company match.
  • Robust medical and life insurance packages that offer a variety of coverage options to meet your individual needs. Travel insurance is also available in certain countries/locations.
  • Opportunities to learn and grow through training and mentoring, work experiences, community involvement and team building.
  • Workplace culture empowering role-based flexibility to maximize personal productivity and balance personal needs.
  • Competitive yearly vacation allowance.
  • Paid time off for new parents (birthing and non-birthing, including adoptive and foster parents).
  • Paid time off to care for family members who are sick or injured.
  • Paid time off to support volunteering and Employee Resource Group’s (ERG) participation.
  • Wellbeing Portal for all Dow employees, our one-stop shop to promote wellbeing, empowering employees to take ownership of their entire wellbeing journey.
  • On-site fitness facilities to help stay healthy and active (availability varies depending on location).
  • Employee discounts for online shopping, cinema tickets, gym memberships and more.
  • Additionally, some of our locations might offer:
    • Transportation allowance (availability varies depending on location)
    • Meal subsidiaries/vouchers (availability varies depending on location)
    • Carbon-neutral transportation incentives e.g. bike to work (availability varies depending on location)

Join our team, we can make a difference together.

About Dow
Dow (NYSE: DOW) is one of the world’s leading materials science companies, serving customers in high-growth markets such as packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer applications. Our global breadth, asset integration and scale, focused innovation, leading business positions and commitment to sustainability enable us to achieve profitable growth and help deliver a sustainable future. We operate manufacturing sites in 30 countries and employ approximately 36,000 people. Dow delivered sales of approximately $43 billion in 2024. References to Dow or the Company mean Dow Inc. and its subsidiaries. ​​​​Learn more about us and our ambition to be the most innovative, customer-centric, inclusive and sustainable materials science company in the world by visiting .

As part of our dedication to inclusion, Dow is committed to equal opportunities in employment. We encourage every employee to bring their whole self to work each day to not only deliver more value, but also have a more fulfilling career. title: Assembly and Test NPI Integrator
description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

Seeking experienced and highly driven individuals to support the Kulim Assembly and Test Manufacturing facility as a New Product Integrator. This role is responsible for coordinating and executing New Product Introduction (NPI) activities to ensure successful product startup from engineering builds through high volume manufacturing (HVM). Responsibilities / Expectations: • Plan and manage NPI execution activities as a product integrator, supporting the development, implementation, and ramp of new technologies or products for external customers. • Act as the primary coordination point for NPI build execution, engaging cross functional teams across engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain to enable successful product startup. • Develop and manage detailed NPI execution plans, including task identification, dependency definition, effort and duration estimation, and project schedule tracking. • Track and publish Performance Against Schedule, ensuring achievement of Critical Success Indicators (CSIs) across key NPI milestones. • Ensure manufacturing readiness by coordinating system setup, process flow definition, material readiness, and capacity availability to support NPI builds and data collection. • Understand product and process challenges and work closely with technical experts across multiple groups to identify solutions and drive Design for Manufacturing (DFM) alignment during NPI execution. • Proactively identify improvement opportunities and support improvement actions to enhance NPI delivery effectiveness, predictability, and quality. • Lead investigation of issues impacting NPI deliverables, perform structured root cause analysis, align risk mitigation actions, and coordinate resolution with responsible functional owners. • Follow up on recovery actions to ensure NPI schedules and sample volume commitments are met with acceptable quality. • Document NPI readiness and deliverables, including process flow, build routing, BOM, and qualification artifacts, and support preparation of factory certification qualification documentation.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications Qualifications • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or an equivalent technical field. • Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in NPI, manufacturing, technology transfer, or related engineering roles. • Knowledge of Assembly and/or Test processes, TD transfer methodologies, and statistical data analysis. • Strong collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively in cross functional teams. • Good English verbal and written communication skills. • Ability to manage multiple priorities with strong organizational and project coordination skills. • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is a plus.

title: Security Coordinator
description:
Job descriptions may display in multiple languages based on your language selection.

What we offer:

At Magna, you can expect an engaging and dynamic environment where you can help to develop industry-leading automotive technologies. We invest in our employees, providing them with the support and resources they need to succeed. As a member of our global team, you can expect exciting, varied responsibilities as well as a wide range of development prospects. Because we believe that your career path should be as unique as you are.

Group Summary:

Cosma provides a comprehensive range of body, chassis and engineering solutions to global customers. Through our robust product engineering, outstanding tooling capabilities and diverse process expertise, we continue to bring lightweight and innovative products to market.

Job Responsibilities:

Assists with the Occupational Health and Safety programs and ensures compliance with accepted safety standards and applicable legislation. Provides instruction and training on safe handling of products, materials and/or equipment. Investigates and reports workplace accidents. Actively participates in the activities of the Joint Health and Safety Committee. Conducts routine audits to determine the nature and extent of unsafe work practices and recommends corrective action. Makes recommendations concerning compliance with all applicable Health & Safety regulations.


Security Operations

  • Plan, implement, and manage security programs for the facility and grounds within a manufacturing environment.
  • Coordinate and conduct regular walk-throughs and security checks across all shifts, 365 days a year, and develop the weekly schedule, including time allocated to each shift.
  • Provide specialized security for, and control access to, limited and restricted areas.
  • Inspect and maintain security infrastructure, including guard shacks, traffic control barriers, and the physical fencing surrounding the 145-acre property, and coordinate repairs with Facilities Maintenance as needed.
  • Identify and lead projects that strengthen site security while delivering cost savings.

Access Control

  • Manage site access through key control and the RFID access control system (employee badges).
  • Develop and continuously improve the door key schedule and the key request and management process, including modifying door hardware as needed.

Contractor and Visitor Management

  • Develop and improve processes to verify that contractors and visitors meet all prerequisite requirements before being granted site access.
  • Responsible for visitor and contractor training and safety protocols

Emergency Preparedness and Response

  • Partner with local emergency agencies (fire, EMS, and police) to ensure BGM is proactively prepared for emergencies.
  • Continuously improve the site’s Emergency Action Plan.
  • Assist in developing and strengthening the site Emergency Response Team (ERT).
  • Routinely inspect emergency evacuation routes and immediately correct any safety concerns.
  • Complete accident and incident investigations within 24 hours, identifying root cause and corrective actions.
  • Provide ongoing workplace violence prevention training to team members.

Communications Systems

  • Assist IT with the issuance and programming of two-way radios and the maintenance of the radio system.

Security Team Leadership

  • Partner with the contract security provider on the interviewing, hiring, and onboarding of security staff, and provide site-specific training.
  • Oversee the daily workflow, schedules, and assignments of security staff, including security guards and desk clerks.
  • Develop and deliver training for new hires and current staff, including workplace searches, drug and alcohol procedures, and related safety and security topics.

Qualifications:

  • Extensive knowledge of security protocols and procedures.
  • Strong management and supervisory skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to train others on security policies and procedures.
  • Ability to handle confidential and classified information.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite or related software.
  • Experience with RFID access control systems and badge management.
  • Knowledge of key control and locksmith practices, including door hardware.
  • Emergency Response Team (ERT) training or experience preferred.
  • Current CPR and first aid certification (or ability to obtain within 90 days of hire).
  • Knowledge of CTPAT preferred.

Education/Experience:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; bachelor’s degree preferred.
  • Five years of related security experience required.

Awareness, Unity, Empowerment:

At Magna, we believe that a diverse workforce is critical to our success. That’s why we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We hire on the basis of experience and qualifications, and in consideration of job requirements, regardless of, in particular, color, ancestry, religion, gender, origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability or gender identity. Magna takes the privacy of your personal information seriously. We discourage you from sending applications via email or traditional mail to comply with GDPR requirements and your local Data Privacy Law.

As part of our commitment to a fair, consistent, and efficient recruitment process, we may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in the initial screening of applications submitted through our Workday system. Job Description:

Reporting to the Commandant for the LSU Corps of Cadets, the Assistant to the Corps of Cadets is responsible for managing the Corps of Cadets leadership day-to-day calendar, strategic project management, and providing general administrative support. The Assistant to the Corps of Cadets provides daily assistance to the Commandant with project management, supporting Corps of Cadets operations, and plays a key role in organizing priorities and supporting strategic initiatives.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES FOR THIS POSITION INCLUDE:

  • Manages the day-to-day calendars, scheduling, and administrative duties for leadership for the Corps of Cadets.
  • Hires, trains, and supervises student employees, leads office functions.
  • Coordinates business and financial operations by processing travel documents, procurement requests, purchasing card transactions, requisitions, invoices, Foundation requests, deposits, and other administrative paperwork.
  • Serves as point of contact for Corps of Cadets for faculty, staff and students internal and external to the department.
  • Support recruitment and cadet operations by assisting with recruitment events and presentations, coordinating Cadets uniform services, and assisting with planning large scale events.

OPPORTUNITIES FOR LEADERSHIP:

Enhance customer service through elevating student employee training and supervision


As the University rebuilds the LSU Corps of Cadets, student employees will play a vital role in the daily operations of the Corps. Through strong supervision and management, delegation and performance management, the Assistant to the Corps of Cadets has an opportunity to set a new standard for customer excellence for everyone who visits our office. As such, it will be necessary to implement new ways of selecting and training student employees, developing intentional onboarding, processes for ensuring quality standards are met, and improving student employee supervision and accountability.

Develop and Optimize Departmental Processes


The Assistant to the Corps of Cadets will help create systems to facilitate productivity and efficiency for the reestablished Corps of Cadets. Managing workflow processes, organizing office procedures, handling deadlines, and establishing efficient systems that the entire Corps staff can rely on will be critical to future success.

Cultivate Strategic Relationships


LSU is an institution that prioritizes relationships. The Assistant to the Corps of Cadets will cultivate strategic relationships while often serving as a bridge between the Commandant, other faculty and staff members, students in the Corps, and the student body.

ATTRIBUTES OF THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE:

A collegial team player who actively builds authentic and mutually-beneficial relationships, who is able to navigate complex organizations and who maintains a good attitude.

Possesses the ability to guide and manage executive leaders efficiently, helping them to identify ways to maximize their effectiveness.

Comfortable with setting organizational standards for professionalism through daily interactions for students.

Confidently provide administrative insights and close student-feedback loops up to the Commandant to support higher-level strategic planning and policy implementation.

Adeptly help solve problems at the lowest level possible.

Maintains attention to detail, is organized, and learns to anticipate needs of others.

Communicate effectively with a wide-range of constituents in-person and in writing.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Administrative Support (60%): Manages the day-to-day calendars, scheduling, and administrative duties for Corps of Cadets administrators specifically the Commandant and Deputy Commandant. This includes: project management, coordinating travel, procurement, and preparing and processing paperwork related to travel, events, p-card, requisitions, invoices, Foundation check requests, and deposits. Serves as the confidential administrative assistant to the Commandant. Manages project workflow processes for the completion of time-sensitive work performed by Corps of Cadets. Oversees office contact with visitors, students and staff, including directing callers and visitors to appropriate staff/resources and ensuring front desk coverage during University business hours. Reviews correspondence/telephone calls related to urgent/confidential matters and determines appropriate action to be taken. Supervises, trains, and oversees all functions regarding student employees. Serves as asset custodian and property management for the Corps of Cadets.

Supply Operations, Event Planning, Recruitment, and Support (30%): Assists planning all Corps of Cadets events including scheduling, planning, processing paperwork and payments, and leading day of arrangements including but not limited to LSU Salutes, Chancellors Parade, Cadet Orientation week, and Parent's Weekend. Supports Corps of Cadets recruitment including assisting with open house presentations and recruiting events. Initiates, coordinates, and oversees laundry, dry-cleaning, and alteration services for Corp uniforms.

Quality Control (5%): Ensures all work, including administrative tasks, implementation, and communications, meets a high standard of quality. Embraces and executes the marginal gains approach and seeks to increase level of all services, events, programs, and experiences in department for continuous improvement every academic year.

Other Duties as Assigned (5%): Other duties as assigned by the Commandant and Deputy Commandant. This includes but is not limited to: efforts that support broad division/institution efforts including at least 40 hours per year spent helping divisional initiatives such as Move-In Day, Welcome Week, Family Weekend, Career Expo, Disability Services Finals Testing, other special projects etc.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:


  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution of higher education.
  • LSU values skills, experience, and expertise. Candidates who have relevant experience in key job responsibilities are encouraged to apply— a degree is not required as long as the candidate meets the required years of experience specified in the job description.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:


  • Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited institution of higher education.
  • One year of working in an office setting.
  • Military experience.
  • Experience managing senior level employees calendars, project management, or systems for meeting planning.

OTHER REQUIREMENTS/EXPECTATIONS:

This position may be asked to work during an official closure, but who is otherwise not required to report to the physical campus during a closure and whose absence does not present a risk to the safety, resources, and well-being of the campus per FASOP HR-01.

As with all LSU employees, due to this position title and/or responsibilities, this position has an obligation to assist students in the acquisition of necessary services. Should a student appear in need of or seek assistance with issues of an emotional, behavioral, or mental health-related matter, they should be referred to the proper service within the Student Health Center. In situations where the student creates an impression that they are a danger to themselves or others, the advisor should immediately contact the Assistant Dean for Care, the Dean of Students, or the appropriate law enforcement agency. The employee, outside of those rights contained within FERPA, should create no impression of client or patient confidentiality.

title: Publishing Specialist II - Regulatory Document Specialist
description:
Publishing Specialist II - Regulatory Document Specialist

Syneos Health® is a leading fully-integrated life sciences services organization built to accelerate customer success. We partner with innovators at every point across the drug development and commercialization continuum, helping them navigate complexity, anticipate change and accelerate progress.

Our Clinical Solutions team members act with a drug development mindset, applying their years of experience and deep expertise to truly understand customer needs and represent those in the solutions we shape.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to deliver – for one another, our customers, and, most importantly, for those in need.

Discover what your 25,000 future colleagues already know:

Why Syneos Health
• We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
• We are committed to building an inclusive culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Central to this is our purpose – Driven to Deliver – which captures the passion of our colleagues to show up each day and shape solutions that have the ability to dramatically impact someone’s life.
• We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because we know that when we bring together smart colleagues from across the world, we can shape the future of healthcare, driving impact for customers and defining the pace of patient progress.

Job Responsibilities

  • 2+ years of Regulatory Publishing experience
  • Hands-on experience with global eCTD submissions and document formatting
  • Strong knowledge of ICH guidelines and eCTD compliance
  • Proficiency in publishing tools such as eCTDManager, Extedo, and Veeva RIM
  • Mandatory experience in Regulatory Publishing and submissions
  • Medical Writing and Regulatory Affairs profiles will not be considered

Essential Functions:

1. Performs Assembler tasks within the document publishing system, including, but not limited to, creating publications, modifying outline, assigning and transforming documents, and adding cross references.

2. Performs Publishing tasks within the electronic publishing system, including, but not limited to, adding special sheets, applying rules, preparing for publishing, and publishing.

3. Performs QC tasks within the electronic publishing system and QC of the published output. May QC materials prepared by team or client.

4. May create, key, and assemble client deliverable documents and submissions using standard word processing or publishing systems and utilities (InSight Publisher, CoreDossier, ISIToolbox, Acrobat).

5. Takes lead role in preparing full application submission builds.

6. Troubleshoots issues with eCTD builds and provide guidance to the entry level puslishers

7. Provides assistance and guidance to entry-level publishers.

8. May review documents for legibility, completeness, and accuracy.

9. May log and track regulatory documents, publications, and other relevant materials.

10. May organize and compile regulatory documentation, perform pagination, clean-up, and duplication tasks.


11. Hand delivers dossier to FDA document room as requried by the clients and submission deadlines.

12. May receive and deliver client information/documents, with significant supervision.

13. May provide alternatives for completing assigned tasks.


  • Prepares and assembles applications (INDs, NDAs, ANDAs, DMFs, etc.) for submission to the FDA.

Other Responsibilities:

Performs other work-related duties as assigned. Minimal travel may be required (up to 25%).

Requirements:

BA/BS with preference given to a science degree. Moderate experience in an office environment, with preference given to drug/device/biologic-related industry, and experience with electronic publishing of regulatory submissions. Experience with relevant software such as InSight Publisher, Documentum, CoreDossier, Ezsubs, ISI Toolbox, MS Word for Windows, and Access. Good knowledge of medical/scientific terminology and/or FDA regulations and procedures. Good communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills. Ability to work independently and to understand and carry out detailed instruction. Attentive to the detail and accuracy of information. Ability to work concurrently on several projects, each with specific instructions that may differ from project to project.

Get to know Syneos Health


Over the past 5 years, we have worked with 94% of all Novel FDA Approved Drugs, 95% of EMA Authorized Products and over 200 Studies across 73,000 Sites and 675,000+ Trial patients.

No matter what your role is, you’ll take the initiative and challenge the status quo with us in a highly competitive and ever-changing environment. Learn more about Syneos Health.

description:
Department:

Full time

Worker Type:

Minimum Requirements:

Bachelor's degree in a related field or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Grade 5 (Hourly)

Position Description:

The Research Grants Coordinator IV in the College of Arts and Sciences will maintain financial records and management of budgets for the EAT lab’s externally funded grant portfolio. The coordinator will also be responsible for assisting EAT Lab faculty with their grant submissions which are focused on risk factors for and treatment of eating disorders. The Research Grants Coordinator IV will work closely with Dr. Levinson and the Research Grants Specialist I to serve as a coordinator for pre-award and post-award tasks for NIH, NSF, DOD, and other internal and external funded submissions.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assist Dr. Levinson and other EAT Lab personnel with post-award initiatives including:
    • Manage ongoing financial tracking and reporting.
    • Collaborate with sponsored programs to facilitate award setup once the Notice of Award (NOA) has been received and ensure university and sponsor compliance.
    • Monitor compliance and submit review reports to funding agencies.
    • Identify and resolve management, financial, and administrative issues.
    • Complete budget projections.
    • Assist with yearly project reports.
    • Maintain financial reports on the grant portfolio of the EAT lab.
    • Maintain university compliance by updating costing for EAT Lab faculty upon changes to their grant portfolio.
    • Collaborate with other departments to set up PSCs, NDAs, Vendor agreements, to ensure collaborators and consultants on grants are registered in the system.
    • Review invoices to ensure accuracy and timely payments.
    • Assist with JIT requests from sponsors prior to award issuance.
    • Prepare and submit requests for NCE (no-cost extensions) and rebudgeting.
    • Review and submit costing updates for lab staff and bi-annual effort reports.
  • Assist Dr. Levinson and other EAT Lab personnel with grant proposal submissions including:
    • Draft grant submission documents including, but not limited to budget, budget justifications, letters of support, current and pending support documents, and biosketches.
    • Review and evaluate grant applications in response to program and Request for Application requirements.
    • Conduct financial reviews of proposed budget costs and budget justifications to ensure accuracy.
    • Develop timelines and tracking systems. Collaborate with sponsored programs to ensure timely submission.
    • Coordinate with external institutions to obtain required documents for proposals containing subawards.
    • Upload documents into federal and non-federal grant systems (e.g., Grants.gov, eRA Commons, ASSIST, Cayuse S2S, and nonprofit foundation systems).
  • Maintain current knowledge of grant regulations and current funding opportunities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Degree in business, accounting, finance, psychology, public health, sociology (or related field). and one or more years of related experience.
  • Experience working with faculty/students or in an academic setting.
  • Familiarity with university or nonprofit budgeting, tracking, and other procedures and requirements.

Competencies

  • Demonstrated ability to work to a deadline.
  • Ability to manage finances and budget documents.
  • Proficiency in communication, budgeting/finance, project management, and federal grant systems (e.g., Grants.gov, eRA Commons, ASSIST, Cayuse, Workday Finance).
  • Strong demonstration of competency to read, comprehend, and apply complex Request for Proposal requirements.
  • Ability to understand, execute, and track grant and contractual requirements towards ensuring financial compliance with sponsor requirements.
  • Strong attention to detail to ensure financial/transaction accuracy.
  • Project Management - organized, task oriented, ability to delegate and follow up with study personnel, sponsored programs administration, and the institutional review board. focus to implement and monitor a complex set of deliverables and deadlines.
  • Proactive - anticipates and plans for problems before they arise.
  • Analytical- evaluating data and other information with the ability to choose the best solution and make recommendations.
  • Flexible – ability to change directions as needed for the good of the laboratory.
  • Service Excellence – responsive, informs constituents of process, pleasant to work with, educates and provides timely, accurate information.
  • Organized – manages time effectively, keeps tasks appropriately prioritized.
  • Critical Thinking – ability to think through issues and identify appropriate options.
  • Work Ethic – motivated, diligent, industrious and persistent in the workplace, stays on tasks to completion, works at a fast pace to ensure optimal efficiency.
  • Interpersonal – can build effective, strong working relationships with laboratory principal investigator and co-investigators, laboratory staff, graduate students, undergraduate research assistants, external collaborators, and the National Institutes of Health through trust, communication, and credibility.
  • Teamwork – ability to work with others, serve others, help others, lead others, mentor others, take directions from others in the interest of moving processes forward to the desired outcome.

title: General Manager II - Store 7883 - Bogart, GA
description:
Job Description

What is a General Manager?

A General Manager must be committed to inspiring our team, helping our Customers succeed and growing our business with integrity. Professional level sales and management position capable of supporting functions on both sides of the business. The role requires understanding of store systems, automotive systems, parts knowledge and has the ability to identify, troubleshoot and project assist for DIY. Responsible for developing and maintaining Professional Customer relationships and program growth. Is accountable for achieving financial metrics and maintaining service and appearance standards. Position is exempt and requires a minimum of 50-55 hours per week (excluding meal break periods). The average schedule is 5-6 days a week, 11 hour shifts, including rotating nights and weekends, with an hour for lunch. Additional hours may be required based on staffing, store conditions, sales to target, and other business demands. General Managers are required to work a schedule based on the needs of the business.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Achieve overall store sales goals and service objectives
  • Manage and grow Professional Customer relationships/sales, including building and holding team accountable to executing Customer action plans
  • Selection, hiring, development, performance mgmt., coaching, scheduling and engagement of store Team Members
  • Ensure execution of all inventory and operational standards
  • Coach all Team Members to deliver on Customer expectations (DIY and Professional)
  • Manager on duty responsibilities (touch base/coaching, floor/phone mgmt., task assignment and completion, safety, open/close duties)
  • Ability to lead change management
  • Embrace diversity and foster a respectful environment for both Customers and Team Members

Secondary Responsibilities

  • Provide DIY service including battery installation, testing, wiper install, etc.
  • Assist District/Region in other functions upon request

Success Factors

  • Friendly communication
  • Ability to locate and stock parts
  • Safety knowledge and skills
  • Ability to become ASE P2 certified or ASE ready equivalent
  • Ability to execute and train project and product quality recommendations
  • Advanced parts lookup and sourcing
  • Ability to source from numerous places including special order, FDO, second source, etc.
  • Ability to execute and train all store operational processes and procedures, and testing and diagnostic equipment for DIY services
  • Ability to execute and train inventory systems and store equipment
  • Ability to execute and train POS and Parts lookup systems
  • Ability to review and analyze P&L statement
  • Ability to recruit, select, hire and develop quality Team Members
  • Ability to build and grow relationships with Professional Customers

Essential Job Skills Necessary for Success as a General Manager

  • Working knowledge of automotive systems preferred
  • Speak and write English (Spanish a plus); communicate effectively and build strong relationships with Customers, peers and upper management
  • Use Microsoft software effectively (Word, Excel required; PowerPoint preferred)
  • Calculate figures and amounts such as discounts, percentages, sales increases, and gross profit percent
  • Ability to review and analyze business reports, such as profit and loss statement (P&L)
  • Hold others accountable, inspect work quality and give feedback in a way that is inspiring
  • Ability to work an assortment of days, evenings and weekends as needed
  • Prior Experience that Sets a General Manager up for Success
  • 2-3 years of experience managing a team of 10 - 20 Team Members in a fast-paced and highly dynamic retail environment
  • Successful experience managing profitability; proven financial and business acumen

Education

  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED), Bachelor’s degree in business or a related area preferred.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations

  • Must have a valid driver's license
  • ASE certification preferred, but not required

Physical Demands

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will predominantly be walking or standing. The employee is required to be able to talk and hear, and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is usually working inside; however, they will occasionally be outside and exposed to various weather conditions while performing such tasks as installing batteries and wiper blades. The employee is also occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts; high, precarious places; toxic or caustic chemicals; risk of electrical shock; explosives; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Position is eligible for sales commission based on individual or store performance.

title: Health Navigator
description:
We are hiring a Health Navigator at BCBST!


In this role, you will support BlueCare Plus Clinical Support at BCBST by serving as a key point of contact for members navigating their healthcare needs. You will assist members by answering questions, completing Health Risk Assessments, and ensuring timely, accurate support through both phone interactions and administrative coordination.

This position combines inbound and outbound phone support with clerical responsibilities, allowing you to engage directly with members while also supporting operational workflows that contribute to effective care delivery. You will work closely with members to understand their needs, provide guidance, and help them access appropriate services and resources.

You will play an important role in improving the overall member experience by delivering compassionate, member-centered support, responding to inquiries with empathy, and helping ensure smooth coordination of care. Responsibilities also include documenting interactions, supporting team processes, and contributing to improved member engagement and satisfaction.

The ideal candidate has experience in a medical office setting or working with senior populations. Success in this role requires strong communication skills, patience, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently. Familiarity with medical terminology is preferred.

We foster a culture where innovation is encouraged. That includes using AI enabled tools responsibly to support everyday work — guided by proven workflows, templates, and policies. As roles become more advanced, we expect employees to leverage AI more broadly to transform how we serve members.


Note:

  • This is a remote role within a collaborative and supportive team environment
  • Schedule: Weekly Rotating shifts of 7:30–4:00 p.m., 8:00–4:30 p.m., 8:30–5:00 p.m. and 9:00-5:30 p.m. EST
  • Overtime may be required based on business needs

Job Responsibilities

  • Conducting educational telephone calls advising members of available benefits, services and programs; completes health needs assessment, and refers members to population health management programs as appropriate.
  • Reaching out to members with identified gaps in care; encouraging and motivating them to become compliant; offering assistance in locating providers and appointment scheduling.
  • Managing system work queues; screening identified members for eligibility, prior case activities, recent claims, customer service inquiries and authorization history; assigning members to clinical team for call outreach and intervention.
  • Facilitating research and analysis of inquiries and/or complaints related to processes and designations, member lost incentives, and other program related inquiries.
  • Work overtime as needed
  • Various immunizations and/or associated medical tests may be required for this position.
  • This job requires digital literacy assessment.

Job Qualifications

Education

description:

Job Category

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

About the Role

The Global Renewals Advisory team is seeking a seasoned Product Renewals Partner to serve as the executive-level renewals advisor to Salesforce Product Leadership for Tableau/Analytics or Informatica or Agentforce/DataCloud . This is a highly visible, cross-functional leadership role that pairs deep renewals and product expertise with senior-executive presence, strategic judgment and the ability to influence product strategy, investment, pricing, and roadmap decisions through the lens of retention.


You will own the renewals narrative for your assigned product portfolio and serve as a strategic thought-partner to the Product Leadership — shaping how GMs, COOs, and their leadership teams understand where retention will land, what is driving attrition and how to mitigate it. You will also partner closely with Forecasting Excellence, Data & Analytics, Pricing & Packaging, and OU-aligned Performance & Strategy teams to bring together a coherent, product-level view of the renewals business and translate it into signals Product can act on.


Responsibilities

Executive Partnership & Advisory

  • Serve as the trusted renewals partner and single point of contact for assigned Product Leadership Teams (GM, COO, CRO, CCO) — building senior-level relationships and earning a seat at the table on strategic decisions.
  • Represent the renewals point of view in Product Leadership Team calls, Monthly and Quarterly Business Reviews, Forecast Reviews, and Executive Reviews.
  • Translate attrition data, forecasts, and trends into strategic implications — framing trade-offs and proposing mitigation strategies that inform product strategy, investment prioritization, pricing, and roadmap decisions.
  • Build fluency in retention across the Product organization so it becomes a shared lens — not a Renewals-only conversation.
  • Communicate risk clearly and take the lead in developing resolution strategies across your assigned product portfolio.

Strategic Analysis & Insight

  • Own the state-of-product-renewals narrative for your assigned portfolio — backward and forward view of retention health, with sharp point-of-view on what the numbers mean.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert for unique areas of the Renewals business, providing expert support to Renewal Managers, including joining customer calls as needed.
  • Bring deep product knowledge to the analysis — understand the nuances of the cloud (pricing model, packaging, product lifecycle, competitive dynamics, customer adoption patterns).
  • Provide best practices on contract structuring to support business and customer needs, including SELA/AELA structuring.

Leadership & Influence

  • Exercise seasoned judgment on complex, ambiguous, and highly visible situations — independently framing recommendations for senior audiences.
  • Contribute to the operating rhythm of the Product Advisory function — shaping deliverables, standards, and best practices as the team scales.

Minimum Requirements

  • 8+ years of experience in Renewals, Customer Success, Sales Strategy & Operations, or related roles, with a track record of managing complex, high-value renewal outcomes at Enterprise / Strategic scale.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering with senior executives (VP, SVP, EVP) — comfortable framing recommendations for and influencing senior leaders.
  • Exceptional executive communication, strong presence in the room, ability to distill complex situations into a sharp point of view.
  • Strong analytical judgment — able to interpret forecasts, trends, and attrition data; identify the story in the numbers; and pressure-test assumptions from teams providing the underlying analytics.
  • Proven ability to operate cross-functionally — building consensus across Sales, Product, Data, Finance, Pricing, Legal, and Renewals stakeholders — without direct authority.
  • Deep understanding of the Salesforce Renewals motion and product lifecycle management, deal, and pricing strategies.

Preferred Requirements

  • Deep product expertise in one or more Salesforce clouds, preferably Tableau/Analytics, Informatica and Agentforce/DataCloud.
  • Prior experience as an Advisory Renewals Manager or equivalent Renewals SME role.

About Lloyds Living
Lloyds Living is a residential investment and operational platform focused on increasing access to high-quality, professionally managed homes and investing in the UK housing market for the long term.

As part of Lloyds Banking Group’s broader commitment to housing, Lloyds Living combines investment, development, asset management, property management and customer capabilities to deliver attractive long-term investment outcomes and support the supply of quality homes across the UK.

Job Description

Role purpose

The Investment Director will shape and deliver Lloyds Living’s investment strategy for affordable housing.


The role will lead business development and origination, develop a scalable investment pipeline and direct multidisciplinary deal teams through underwriting, approval and completion. It will play a central role in deploying Lloyds Living’s significant capital commitment into Affordable Housing, while maintaining strong commercial discipline, governance and alignment with the wider Lloyds Living platform.


The Investment Director will lead engagement with the Investment Committee and work closely with the Lloyds Living For-Profit Registered Provider (FPRP) Board, ensuring that relevant investments support its mandate and are delivered within the appropriate regulatory and governance framework.

Key responsibilities

  • Shape and execute the investment strategy for affordable housing opportunities.
  • Translate Lloyds Living’s strategic objectives and capital commitment into clear investment priorities, criteria and delivery plans.
  • Lead business development and origination, establishing scalable channels and a strong pipeline of high-quality opportunities.
  • Build senior relationships with developers, housebuilders, registered providers, landowners, local authorities, advisers and investment partners.
  • Lead the assessment, underwriting, structuring, negotiation and execution of complex transactions.
  • Direct multidisciplinary deal teams across Investment, Legal, Tax, Finance, Risk, Development, Asset Management and Operations.
  • Ensure investment recommendations are supported by robust commercial analysis, appropriate due diligence and a clear assessment of risk and return.
  • Lead deal teams through the Investment Committee and other relevant approval processes, presenting clear and decision-focused recommendations.
  • Work closely with the Lloyds Living FPRP Board and its committees, ensuring relevant investments are consistent with the Board’s mandate, strategic priorities and regulatory responsibilities.
  • Provide the FPRP Board with clear and timely information to support effective oversight, challenge and decision-making.
  • Maintain effective governance and clear accountability across investment origination, recommendation, approval and delivery.
  • Manage relationships with senior stakeholders across Lloyds Living, Lloyds Banking Group and external partner organisations.
  • Integrate the affordable housing strategy with Lloyds Living’s wider investment, asset management, operational and customer platform.
  • Lead, develop and grow a high-performing investment team, allocating resources effectively across competing priorities.

Experience and capabilities

  • At least 10 years’ relevant experience within asset management, principal investment, UK living real estate investment, alternative corporate finance or a related environment.
  • A strong track record of originating, structuring and executing complex investment transactions.
  • Experience leading, developing and growing high-performing teams.
  • Significant experience managing complex senior stakeholder relationships and presenting to boards, investment committees or equivalent decision-making forums.
  • Strong commercial, financial and risk judgement, with the ability to balance pace of execution with disciplined underwriting and governance.
  • Strong experience in affordable housing investment, including the origination, structuring and execution of transactions with registered providers, housebuilders, developers or local authorities, is preferred.
  • An understanding of the governance and regulatory considerations associated with a for-profit registered provider or regulated housing platform would be advantageous.
  • A pragmatic, positive and collaborative leadership style, with a strong bias to action and the ability to create clarity, make sound decisions and maintain momentum through the ambiguity of a growing business.
  • CFA, CAIA, ACA candidates preferred.

title: Senior Engineering Manager
description:
Impact

The Senior Engineering Manager – Marketing, Incentive Platform & CMS role is a senior people and technology leader within Shipt’s Member Marketplace and Marketing engineering organization. This role reports directly to the Director of Engineering and is responsible for leading a multi-disciplinary group of 10+ backend, web, and mobile engineers across multiple agile pods.

This leader oversees the core capabilities powering Shipt’s promotional marketing ecosystem, customer segmentation, multi-channel campaign orchestration, and Content Management System (CMS) tooling. Driving long-term technical strategy, engineering excellence, delivery predictability, and team health across diverse experiences, the Senior Engineering Manager operates with broader ownership, deeper architectural influence, higher cross-functional visibility, a wider breadth of stakeholders, and increased responsibility for scaling teams, managing complex initiatives, and shaping engineering culture.

Senior Engineering Managers collaborate closely with Staff & Principal Engineers, Product Managers, UX Designers & Managers, Data Scientists, Marketing & Merchandising Operations, and partner engineering teams to execute against multi-quarter roadmaps, strengthen engineering fundamentals, develop talent to meet engineering expectations of the next level, remove organizational bottlenecks, and guide engineers through ambiguity with clarity and strategic direction.

This is a high-impact role that requires strong technical depth, exceptional leadership maturity, strategic decision-making, and the ability to steward mission-critical tech assets and engineering teams through platform modernization, peak retail readiness, and AI-driven transformation.

What You’ll Need to Be Successful

Strategic Technical Leadership
  • Lead and influence architectural direction across full-stack domains, including high-concurrency backend microservices (Golang, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, Snowflake, GraphQL/Apollo Federation) and frontend/CMS experiences (React, React Native, Server/Client-Driven UI).
  • Partner with Engineering, Product, UX, Data Science, and Marketing/Merchandising Operations leaders to define multi-quarter modernization plans, system migrations, quality bars, and domain boundaries across promotions, audience targeting, campaign orchestration, and CMS authoring tools.
  • Ensure teams consistently adopt modern engineering practices, including event-driven patterns, real-time budget and state-machine orchestration, deep observability, performance optimization for peak retail traffic, and AI-assisted development.
  • Oversee the technical strategy for your areas of responsibility, ensuring alignment with Shipt- or department-wide architectural principles and long-term company goals.
  • Drive cross-team technical initiatives that improve stability, reliability, and operational excellence across complex, interconnected services (e.g., Campaign Navigator, Order & Membership Promotions, Audience Builder/Delivery, and CMS platforms).

Cross-Discipline Leadership
  • Own end-to-end delivery for customer-facing promotional experiences, internal marketing/CMS tooling, and core backend capabilities, ensuring predictable execution against roadmaps, OKRs, and quarterly commitments.
  • Lead technical planning cycles — capacity planning, dependency mapping across frontend/backend pods, long-range planning, and risk mitigation.
  • Establish unified prioritization and intake frameworks that protect engineering focus, minimize context-switching, and streamline cross-functional requests.
  • Establish processes that improve productivity, throughput, rollout safety, code quality, and release cadence (including CI/CD modernization).
  • Ensure high operational readiness across all owned services — SLOs, observability instrumentation (Grafana, DataDog, Rollbar), dashboards, runbooks, on-call rotations, and proactive peak-season load testing.

People Leadership & Organizational Scaling
  • Manage 10+ engineers across backend, web, and mobile disciplines, spanning mid-level to Staff levels.
  • Guide career development through structured mentorship, progression frameworks, and personalized growth plans — actively developing Senior engineers into tech leads and Staff engineers, and supporting Staff engineers stepping into broader organizational influence.
  • Establish high talent density through strong hiring, rigorous performance management, and targeted mentorship programs.
  • Scale and size teams sustainably, anticipating skill gaps, capacity needs, and future organizational structures across Incentive Platform and CMS pods.
  • Build and reinforce a culture of high accountability, ownership, and continuous improvement toward the demonstration of Shipt Values.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management & Influence
  • Serve as the primary engineering partner to Product, UX, Data Science, Growth Marketing, and Retailer Operations for your areas of responsibility.
  • Translate product strategy, internal marketing user needs, and business outcomes into clear technical direction and execution plans.
  • Influence prioritization and sequencing decisions across competing stakeholder backlogs through strong technical judgment and data-driven reasoning.
  • Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders across Member Marketplace, Checkout & Pricing, Personalization, Loyalty, Infrastructure, and Data Science.
  • Communicate progress, risks, blockers, trade-offs, and decisions — early, clearly, and often — to executive leaders and cross-functional partners.

Engineering Excellence & Continuous Improvement
  • Champion AI-assisted engineering practices — expanding the use of AI coding assistants, automated test agents, refactoring agents, and intelligent developer workflows (e.g., automated ticket/spec generation and support workflows).
  • Improve engineering fundamentals across code quality, testing maturity, observability, scalability, and architectural hygiene.
  • Establish and continuously improve product team working agreements drawing from expertise and experience with multiple agile software development methodologies.
  • Lead and refine agile ceremonies (e.g., sprint planning, cross-pod backlog refinement, demos, retrospectives) to ensure crisp acceptance criteria and cross-pod alignment.
  • Lead post-incident reviews and systemic corrective action initiatives across multiple teams.

title: Senior Compliance Consultant
description:
The Senior Compliance Consultant is a senior subject matter expert and leader providing compliance advisory and independent oversight support to the Canada Segment Individual Insurance, Group Benefits and Affinity businesses.

The role interprets complex regulatory requirements, serves as an escalation point for compliance matters, supports oversight and monitoring activities, and collaborates with business and oversight partners on cross-segment and global initiatives. Leveraging extensive industry, regulatory, product, distribution, and operational expertise, the role provides practical, risk-based guidance, promotes consistent compliance practices, strengthens risk management capabilities, and influences stakeholders across multiple business and oversight functions.


Position Responsibilities:


· Develop, implement, and maintain compliance programs, policies, procedures, and oversight activities that help the Canada Segment Individual Insurance and Affinity businesses meet regulatory and risk-based compliance requirements.

· Interpret legislation, regulations, industry rules, guidelines, regulatory expectations, and emerging risks, and translate requirements into clear, practical guidance for business partners and compliance colleagues.

· Serve as a subject matter expert and escalation point for complex compliance matters, applying independent judgment and providing practical, risk-based recommendations that support informed business decisions.

· Lead or coordinate significant compliance initiatives, regulatory change implementation activities, compliance reviews, control testing, and other oversight activities involving multiple stakeholders.

· Use AI-enabled tools, data analytics, reporting insights, automation, and process improvement to improve the speed, quality, consistency, and scalability of compliance oversight, monitoring, and reporting.

· Partner with Compliance, business partners, Legal, Internal Audit, and other oversight partners to drive consistent interpretation, clear ownership, proactive communication, independent challenge, timely escalation, and practical resolution of compliance risks and issues.

· Influence business, project and compliance outcomes through subject matter expertise, effective stakeholder engagement and leadership without direct authority.

· Represent Compliance on business, cross-segment, global, and regulatory initiatives and forums, bringing forward insights into regulatory expectations, emerging risks, and industry practices.

· Assess compliance risks, evaluate the effectiveness of compliance-related controls and procedures, and recommend mitigation, remediation, and control enhancement strategies, including escalation where appropriate.

· Provide informal leadership through mentoring, coaching, knowledge sharing, training and continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen team capability and effectiveness.

· Develop and deliver targeted compliance training and awareness programs for business partners.

· Prepare, and deliver compliance reporting, metrics, and analysis

· Support audits, regulatory examinations, investigations, and other oversight reviews.


Core Skills & Competencies:

· Strong analytical, investigative, interpretive, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.

· Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex information clearly and concisely to diverse audiences.

· Strong interpersonal and relationship-management skills, with the ability to build credibility and maintain effective relationships across all levels of the organization.

· Excellent organizational, prioritization, and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

· Demonstrated ability to work independently while exercising sound judgment and maintaining a high degree of ownership and accountability.

· Strong project management skills and the ability to lead and coordinate complex initiatives.

· Strong coaching, mentoring, and facilitation skills.

· Ability to use data-driven insights, analytics, and AI-enabled tools to identify trends, prioritize work, improve oversight quality, and support consistent decision-making.

· Ability to collaborate across Compliance teams and first and second line partners to promote shared understanding, proactive communication, consistency, and scalable solutions.

· Demonstrated ability to influence business decisions and drive outcomes through expertise, credibility, and effective stakeholder engagement.

· Strong relationship-management skills with the ability to build trust, challenge constructively, and collaborate across business and oversight functions.

· Proven ability to lead complex initiatives, drive change, and promote continuous improvement without direct authority.

· Enterprise mindset with the ability to consider broader business, customer, regulatory, operational, and reputational impacts.



Strategic Impact & Key Challenges:


· Provide senior-level compliance expertise, leadership and influence that supports business enablement, effective risk management, and consistent application of the compliance framework.

· Anticipate and assess emerging regulatory developments, compliance risks, and cross-functional impacts, translating them into practical and scalable oversight responses.

· Leverage analytics, AI-enabled tools, automation, and process improvements to enhance compliance oversight and decision making.

· Balance business objectives with regulatory obligations by providing sound judgment, and practical solutions in a complex, multi-jurisdictional environment.

· Handle sensitive and complex matters where failure to identify, assess, escalate, or remediate compliance risks could result in regulatory, financial, reputation risks

Required Qualifications:


· 7 + years of progressive compliance experience in the financial services industry, preferably in insurance.

· University degree; industry courses or professional certifications are an asset.

· Advanced knowledge of insurance products, distribution channels, operations, and associated regulatory requirements, industry practices and associated compliance risks.

· Demonstrated professional judgment, integrity, and adherence to high ethical standards.

· Experience using data, analytics, reporting tools, and AI-enabled solutions to support compliance monitoring, oversight, risk assessment, and process improvement.

· Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset. For positions based in Quebec, proficiency in both English and French will be required to support our business partners across Canada.
