title: Production Control Clerk II
description:
Worker Type

Regular


Job Description

Summary

The Production Control Clerk performs clerical tasks in the production control function. One coordinates and controls work orders released to Production as well as goods moving back and forth between Production and Flight Team.


Position Responsibilities

  • Execute material repair orders when necessary to move product from SMRB to the repair work cell.
  • Coordinate and alleviate identified work order part shortages by working closely with Purchasing, Quality and Production Planners.
  • Update and prioritize the rework board in the production area, coordinating with production planners
  • Proactively monitoring and expediting identified shortage parts that are in ‘inspection’ status, through quality, stockroom and onto work orders that are waiting for shortage parts.
  • Working with the production leads to help move urgent product from one cell to another or through the stockroom.
  • Issue items in a timely manner to work orders that are being collected and processed in the sell-off area.
  • Notify planners in a timely manner of rejected, identified shortage parts or rejected production builds.
  • Work with Quality to ensure identified shortage parts do not sit in SMRB for an extraordinarily long period
  • Follows established procedures on routine work and may require instruction on new assignments
  • Maintains a clean and safe work environment
  • Works on assignments that are moderately difficult, requiring judgement in resolving issues
  • Other duties as assigned

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills & Experience)

  • Minimum of 1-2 years of experience in a production environment
  • Hands-on experience with MRP systems, material planning, inventory control and the generation and maintenance of work orders is required
  • Knowledge of computerized MRP systems is critical
  • High School diploma or GED Equivalent required
  • Any APICS training and/or certification is desirable, especially as it pertains to inventory control and material planning

Other Qualifications & Desired Competencies

  • Must have good computer operation skills as well as proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook)
  • Must have strong oral and written communication skills to communicate effectively with employees in the Company
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving skills and attention to detail and strong sense of urgency to meet schedule
  • Receives little instructions on daily work and general instructions on newly introduced assignments
  • Demonstrated ability to make decisions and formulate and execute alternative plans when the need arises
  • Focuses on teamwork, collaboration and puts the success of the team above one's own interests

Physical Demands

  • Ability to work in a manufacturing environment (Constant)
  • Required to sit and stand for long periods; talk, hear, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer and telephone keyboard (Constant)
  • Frequently lift and/or carry objects of small size between 2lbs and 5lbs
  • Frequently required to use hand to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls and balance
  • Occasionally required to reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and talk or hear

No Clearance

5 years of relevant experience in technology risk, IT audit, data/AI advisory or consulting, including at least 1 year focused on AI governance, AI risk management or AI solution deliveryo At least 1 year of hands-on experience working with and developing AI products and solutions (e.g. machine learning models, generative AI / LLM-based applications, AI agents), covering the AI lifecycle from use-case definition and data preparation to deployment and monitoringo 3 years of experience in a supervisory/managerial capacity, leading teams and client engagements, including responsibility for title: Canada Reporting Steward Analyst
description:
The Actuarial Systems, Data & Reporting team is seeking an experienced professional to lead Canada Segment Reporting Steward activities. This role will serve as a strategic partner between Canada Actuarial and Technology teams, with a primary focus on driving reporting and process change initiatives and guiding system and process improvements.


The Canada Reporting Steward will coordinate quarter-end reporting readiness, support timely system refreshes and reporting milestones, and address issues through effective troubleshooting, stakeholder coordination, and escalation. A key responsibility will be overseeing the end-to-end valuation change management process, including prioritization, change assessment, JIRA tracking, testing, implementation, and post-implementation follow-up.


In addition to the primary Reporting Steward mandate, this role will support selected Canada Data Steward activities, including data issue investigation, data quality management, data lineage understanding, and governance support.


The ideal candidate will bring strategic thinking, effective collaboration, and a passion for clear documentation and process improvement. Experience with data warehouses, business intelligence tools, and SQL or similar data-querying capabilities would be an asset.


Position Responsibilities:

  • Lead reporting change management by coordinating with Canada Actuarial and Technology teams to collect, assess, prioritize, and oversee change requests.
  • Collaborate with technology and business stakeholders on solution assessments, requirements clarification, delivery planning, and implementation decisions.
  • Maintain and track JIRA epics, stories, defects, enhancement requests, risks, decisions, and implementation items through the full change lifecycle.
  • Represent Canada reporting priorities during assessments of proposed valuation process changes, sprint planning, stand-ups, release planning, and governance discussions.
  • Guide and support teams to ensure the successful implementation of reporting and data solutions in alignment with actuarial reporting requirements and business objectives.
  • Collaborate with the global product owner, delivery partners, and representatives from other segments (U.S. and Asia) to assess global actuarial systems and reporting changes affecting the Canada segment, identify dependencies and downstream impacts, coordinate delivery timing, and engage Canada segment stakeholders in implementation, testing, and approval activities.
  • In partnership with the Canada Segment Scrum Master, facilitate successful Systems Integration Testing (SIT) and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) cycles, ensuring appropriate testing coverage, issue resolution, stakeholder sign-off, production implementation, and quarter-end production readiness.
  • Provide subject matter support, including issue investigation, root-cause analysis, stakeholder coordination, escalation, and resolution tracking.
  • Provide strategic insights and practical recommendations that improve reporting processes, controls, operational efficiency, and production stability.
  • Support process improvements and business intelligence solutions to enhance actuarial analysis and reporting capabilities.
  • Proactively identify opportunities to enhance processes and actuarial reporting, establish practical and sustainable best practices, and translate recurring requests into streamlined, repeatable solutions.
  • Create and maintain clear documentation for reporting processes, projects, testing outcomes, controls, decisions, and recurring procedures.
  • As required, support Data Stewardship activities by assisting with ad hoc data analysis and reconciliations, documenting data findings and adjustments, supporting stakeholder discussions related to data quality and transparency, building knowledge of data flows, and contributing to data change testing preparations.

Required Qualifications:

  • Career ASA/ACIA or actuarial/IT background, with a strong understanding of life insurance and actuarial reporting concepts.
  • 5+ years of experience with increasing responsibilities in life insurance, actuarial reporting, valuation, financial reporting, actuarial systems, data management, or a related technology area.
  • Familiarity with reporting and systems change processes and experience leading or supporting process change requirements, testing, implementation, and production support initiatives.
  • Strong project and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple stakeholders and timelines.
  • Excellent communication, collaboration and leadership abilities, with demonstrated success engaging stakeholders and influencing alignment across teams.
  • Strong analytical and strategic problem-solving skills, including the ability to connect information across systems, processes, and stakeholder groups.
  • Ability to identify risks, dependencies, and downstream implications before they affect reporting timelines or production outcomes.
  • Proactive and self-motivated, with the ability to work independently and effectively in cross-functional teams.
  • Strong documentation skills and a commitment to knowledge sharing, process transparency, and business continuity.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • ASA/ACIA designation.
  • Experience with IFRS 17, valuation reporting, quarter-end financial reporting, or financial controls.
  • Experience with Agile delivery, project management, or structured process change practices.
  • Experience working with actuarial systems, JIRA, and business intelligence tools.
  • Experience developing or reviewing SQL queries for actuarial or financial data analysis.
  • Familiarity with Risk Integrity, Moody’s AXIS, Qlik, Power BI, Databricks, Python, or related tools.
  • An understanding of data quality management, implications of data issues, and ETL concepts.
  • Experience working with offshore development teams or in a distributed, cross-time-zone organization.
  • Project management experience or certification is an asset.

title: Ligand ID Lead, Director  (EMD)
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Position Summary:
The Early Molecule Design team’s mission is to identify hit molecules and advance them to lead optimization and become breakthrough medicines. We are searching for experienced and engaged scientific experts who are recognized authorities in molecular pharmacology and drive the advancement of our portfolio across oncology, immunology, pain, Alzheimer’s, diabetes, and obesity. These positions are for seasoned drug hunters who ask the right scientific questions and collect high-impact data that drives programs forward.

The primary measure of success in this role is portfolio-level impact— resolving the hardest pharmacological questions through hypothesis- and data-driven approaches, delivering the mechanistic and translational insights that change the trajectory of multiple programs, and building the scientific capabilities that raise the ceiling on what Ligand ID can achieve. We are looking for innovative scientists with a strong growth mindset who can challenge dogma and champion breakthrough approaches.

Responsibilities:
Technical / Scientific Contributions: Driving Hit ID to Drug Candidates

  • Serve as a recognized core team expert in ligand identification whose scientific guidance and data strategies directly resolve critical project challenges and advance programs through major milestones.
  • Identify scientific problems limiting program progress, and take personal ownership of driving solutions through thoughtful assay design and execution, mechanistic investigation, and creative pharmacological thinking.
  • Accountable for both the technical functional execution, and facilitating proactive technical strategic planning at project and core team level.
  • Operate with urgency and transparency in surfacing challenges; anticipate scientific risk and proactively adjust team strategy to keep programs moving forward.
  • Driving cross functional strategic and technical planning, at both core team and project team level.
  • Accountable for delivering projects to a go-no go decisions based on strategic and technical experience.
  • Champion breakthrough scientific approaches to portfolio-wide challenges; challenge dogma to uncover new opportunities.
  • Accountable for cross functional strategic decision making across multiple projects and project core teams.
  • Lead rapid conceptualization and realization of innovative small molecule targeting strategies that shape long-term focus areas of the portfolio in a highly competitive landscape

Enabling: Partnerships and Tools That Accelerate Impact

  • Foster an environment that supports open scientific debate and bold, evidence-based decisions.
  • At core team level, provide expert scientific guidance that shapes project strategy and improves probability of technical success.
  • Actively incorporate state-of-the-art methods, including AI/ML, into the group’s scientific workflows.
  • Identify capability gaps — in tools, methods, or scientific approaches — and develop solutions that benefit multiple programs across the portfolio.
  • Build internal and external networks that enhance the capabilities of the Ligand ID team.
  • Identify and contribute to external innovation opportunities that strengthen the portfolio

Supporting: Team Development and Culture

  • Actively mentor and develop diverse scientific talent across sites and functions.
  • Champion a ONE TEAM, SAME TEAM mindset; model radical transparency in surfacing challenges.
  • Provide effective coaching and feedback that develops team members’ ability to deliver higher-impact science.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives that leverage diverse perspectives to drive program outcomes.
  • Serve as a mentor within the division and beyond; invest in building the next generation of scientific leaders.
  • Lead complex initiatives for continuous improvement, process innovation, and adoption of new scientific approaches.

Safety & Compliance — Model Safety Leadership Through Personal Practice

  • Demonstrate an unwavering commitment to safety-first laboratory practice: complete required safety training, conduct risk assessments before experiments, and escalate concerns immediately.
  • Follow all site safety, environmental, and regulatory compliance requirements; actively reinforce a safety-first team culture.

Basic Requirements:

  • PhD in Biochemistry, Biology, Biophysics, Molecular Biology, Pharmacology, or a related field, with at least 7+ years of relevant research and/or industry experience (may include post-doc experience) or MS with 10+ years industry/academic/research or BS with 15+ years industry/academic/research experience.
  • Demonstrated drug hunter experience with a track record of advancing discovery programs.
  • Extensive experience utilizing CROs across the world to expand our capacity to provide specific technical and scientific solutions that increase overall cycle times.
  • Deep scientific background in biochemistry, biophysics, and cell biology to guide ligand identification across modalities.
  • Strong experience leading teams of scientists and achieving cross-disciplinary goals.
  • Team player with a positive, can-do attitude and a commitment to scientific rigor and integrity.

Additional Preferences:

  • Broad experience across multiple biological and small molecule mechanisms, modalities, and therapeutic areas.

title: Store Hardlines Manager #283 - Weatherford, TX
description:
Who We Are

At Academy Sports + Outdoors our vision is to be the best sports + outdoors retailer in the country — but what truly sets us apart is our people. We’re a passionate, purpose-driven team that’s as committed to each other as we are to our customers.

We’ve spent over 80 years building a culture that puts people first. We believe in creating opportunities for growth, fostering meaningful connections, and supporting every Team Member’s journey. What fuels us? Our belief in the power of fun.

Here, you won’t just help customers gear up for their next adventure — you’ll launch one of your own. Whether you're starting out or leveling up, Academy is a place where fun can’t lose!

What You Will Work On

As a Hardlines Manager, you will own the day‑to‑day leadership and execution of some of the store’s most dynamic and high‑impact departments, including Camping, Fishing & Hunting, Outdoor, Firearms, and Team Sports. You’ll translate business priorities into clear actions for your team, ensuring every area is ready to serve customers through strong merchandising, staffing, and operational discipline. Your leadership will directly influence sales results, customer trust, and overall store performance.

You will drive operational excellence by planning labor, coaching leaders, and holding teams accountable to safety, compliance, and service standards. From walking departments and setting priorities to reviewing performance metrics, you’ll balance strategic thinking with hands‑on problem solving. Every day, you’ll turn feedback, data, and observation into improvements that elevate the customer experience and team engagement.

Who You Will Work With

You’ll partner closely with the Store Director and fellow store leaders to align on goals, priorities, and execution strategies. On the floor, you’ll lead and develop Team Leads and Team Members, creating a culture of accountability, trust, and continuous improvement across all hardlines areas.

You’ll also collaborate with cross‑functional partners, including operations and support teams, to ensure compliance, training completion, and consistent standards. Through daily communication and collaboration, you’ll help connect company initiatives to real‑world execution that benefits both customers and team members.

What You Bring

Bring your energy, your ideas, and your love for sports and the outdoors.

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field preferred

  • Minimum of 3 years of relevant leadership or management experience required

  • Demonstrated success leading departments of up to 40 team members while driving operational excellence and achieving sales targets

  • Strong customer focus with a proven commitment to delivering exceptional service

  • Ability to analyze business results and translate insights into action

  • Clear and confident communication skills across diverse audiences

  • Comfort making decisions in a fast‑paced, retail environment

  • Knowledge of operational processes, safety standards, and compliance requirements

  • Ability to complete and maintain required certifications, including Firearms Sales and Power Industrial Truck

  • Comfortably manage and audit firearm sales, ensuring all transactions meet federal and state requirements through accurate completion of ATF Form 4473, background check verification, and final approval

  • A team-first attitude; while your core duties are your priority, you're happy to step in wherever you're needed

Work Style and Physical Requirements

  • Flexibility to work varying schedules, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, based on business needs

  • Full-time position averaging 45-50 hours per week during peak times

  • Capability to remain on your feet and move throughout the store for extended periods during scheduled shifts

  • Ability to perform physical job functions such as walking, bending, reaching, pulling, carrying, and lifting items up to 50 lbs

  • Capacity to complete repetitive tasks, including scanning, stocking, and folding merchandise

  • Comfort using ladders or step stools to access merchandise as needed

  • Ability to thrive in a fast‑paced retail environment while adapting to shifting priorities

  • Acceptable level of hearing and vision to perform job duties

  • Ability to adhere to company policies and professional standards

Key Skills

Operations, Workforce Management, Driving Results, Customer Service, Strategy and Execution

description:

Federal Reserve Bank of DallasWe are dedicated to serving the public by promoting a strong financial system and a healthy economy for all. About the Role:

The Credit Risk and Reserves Analyst supports the Condition Monitoring, Discount Window Lending, Collateral administration, and Reserves functions in the Credit, Risk, and Reserves Management (CRRM) Department. This position will report to the Supervisor of Collateral and Lending in the CRRM Department. The Credit Risk and Reserves Analyst will perform risk assessments on depository institutions, complete master account request reviews, assist with regulator outreach efforts, and provide briefings to management and the department. They may also serve on System and District projects/workgroups that support the department’s functions. The Credit Risk and Reserves Analyst is expected to work under a moderate to limited level of supervision and collaborate with team members to solve problems and moderately-complex requests.

You Will:

  • Under moderate to limited guidance, perform routine to complex operational and analytical duties in assigned area of responsibility.
  • Perform financial analysis on the condition of District depository institutions, including analysis of capital, asset quality, management, earnings performance, and liquidity. Also perform financial analysis of other business entities to determine level of counter-party risk to the Reserve Bank.
  • Analyze account access and financial services requests from eligible institutions in the District. Perform evaluation of new and existing accounts relationships to determine risks to the Reserve Bank, payment system, and financial stability.
  • Complete assigned work products, including risk assessments, account reviews, analysis of depository institution self-assessed net debit caps, and other correspondence to institutions.
  • Communicate with institutions and processes moderately complex requests and questions regarding loan advances, payments, intraday credit, and account administration.
  • Perform operational tasks related to the administration of accounts and payment system risk including problem institution resolution, account openings and closings, structure changes, institutional mergers, monitoring overdraft usage, applying charges, and assisting with counseling institutions.
  • Ensure services delivered to District institutions are efficient, accurate, and timely.
  • Assist with maintaining an effective control environment and ensuring compliance with and enforcement of applicable Federal Reserve rules, guidelines, and regulations.
  • Coordinate with external governance partners during department effectiveness reviews (e.g., internal audit, financial statement audit, Board oversight).
  • Participate in and occasionally lead projects, workgroups, or committees at the department, Reserve Bank, and/or Federal Reserve System level.
  • Maintain an in-depth knowledge of banking laws and regulations, and Board/System policies to respond effectively to inquiries and perform duties according to these mandates.
  • Prepare and sometimes deliver briefings, presentations, recommendations and other communications for key internal and external stakeholders regarding matters impacting key business functions, internal applications, and policy issues.

You Have:

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business or related fields.
  • Must have at least 2-6 years of work experience focused on credit risk, collateral operations, financial analysis, payments, reserves or treasury operations, banking supervision and regulation, or related fields.
  • General to intermediate knowledge of department operations, internal control frameworks (COSO/SOX), banking laws and regulations, and Federal Reserve policies and operating circulars.
  • Experience working for a federal or state regulator as an examiner/risk specialist is a plus.

title: District Manager D 4606 Shreveport LA
description:
Job Description

What is a District Manager?

A District Manager is the senior leader in the district. The District Manager must be knowledgeable of all facets of store operations in order to successfully grow Retail and Commercial market share. Each District Manager must be committed to leading and inspiring our team, helping our DIY and Commercial customers succeed, while growing sales and profitability with integrity.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Achieve or exceed district total sales and profitability goals
  • Ensure commercial customer retention & relationship growth in the market
  • Selection, hiring, development, goal setting, performance mgmt., coaching, engagement and retention of General Managers and Core 4 team members
  • Ensure proper staffing levels throughout the district
  • Ensure execution of all inventory & operational standards within the district
  • Conduct regular store visits providing action plans to achieve full market potential.
  • Teach business acumen by review of profit and loss statement with GM's
  • Communicate effectively and appropriately to stores and support staff
  • Embrace diversity and foster a respectful environment for both customers and team members

Secondary Responsibilities

  • Assist region/area in other functions upon request

Success Factors

  • Knowledge of store operations and processes
  • ASE P2 certified or ASE ready equivalent
  • Ability to recruit, select, hire and develop quality General Managers and ensure same for Core 4 positions
  • Accountability, coaching & feedback skills
  • Ability to execute and train all store operational processes, procedures and team member/customer standards
  • Ability to use and train, testing and diagnostic equipment for DIY services
  • Effectively use Excel, Word, Outlook and PowerPoint computer programs

Essential Job Skills Necessary for Success as a District Manager

  • Working knowledge of automotive systems preferred
  • Speak and write English (Spanish a plus); communicate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, peers and upper management
  • Use Microsoft software effectively (Word, Excel required, PowerPoint preferred)
  • Use basic math accurately: add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals
  • Perform calculations such as Gross Margin and understand financial documents, such as Profit and Loss Statements (P&L), invoices, etc.
  • Ability to fully understand all facets of the business and excel in an integrated operating model (including DIY, Commercial, PDQ and Hub operations)
  • Define problems, collect information, establish facts, draw valid conclusions and effectively resolve issues independently

title: Director Regulatory Intelligence & Policy
description:
Are you ready to turn regulatory intelligence into decisive actions that accelerate breakthrough therapies for patients? As Director Regulatory Intelligence & Policy, you will shape how we read the external environment and convert emerging signals into clear choices for our pipeline and marketed assets in respiratory and immunology. Picture yourself influencing development strategies and labels by bringing timely, high-quality insight to senior leaders and cross-functional teams.

Based at our Gothenburg, Sweden R&D site, you will sit within a strategy-focused team spanning regulatory science, data analytics, and policy. You will lead the translation of guidance changes, precedents, and competitor activity into practical recommendations that shorten timelines, strengthen submissions, and de-risk key decisions. How will you use new evidence, global trends, and AI-enabled analysis to change the course of a program?

Accountabilities:

- Regulatory Landscape Analysis: Monitor and assess evolving guidance, review precedents and approval summaries, and deliver impact analyses that informregulatory strategies and ensure compliance.

- Insight Translation: Convert complex external signals into clear, actionable recommendations that sharpen development pathways, strengthen labels, and accelerate approvals.

- Cross-Functional Intelligence: Partner with Clinical Information Science, Commercial Intelligence, and other experts to align regulatory interpretation with emerging disease area insights and business drivers.

- Strategic Research: Conduct bespoke regulatory research and provide the regulatory intelligence component of disease area and product-specific strategies.

- Internal Collaboration: Work closely with global regulatory strategists, intelligence and policy groups across the enterprise to interpret EMA, FDA, and other Health Authority perspectives and trends.

- External Policy Engagement: Coordinate input on draft guidance and ensure therapy area priorities are reflected in external regulatory policy interactions.

- Global Integration: Liaise with regional regulatory leaders in International, China, and Japan to capture regional nuances and integrate them into a cohesive global view.

- Portfolio Acceleration: Identify opportunities to leverage novel pathways, innovative evidence generation, and new technologies that unlock speed and value across the portfolio.

- AI-Enabled Insight Generation: Identify and implement opportunities to use artificial intelligence and other new tools to simplify processes, increase insight quality, and enhance decision speed.

- Executive Communication: Present concise, influential updates to senior leaders, shaping risk assessments and portfolio choices.

Essential Skills/Experience:

- Advanced degree in a science related field and/or other appropriate knowledge/experience.

- Strong demonstrated ability in regulatory strategy, operations, intelligence or policy.

- Detailed understanding of European regulatory affairs and an understanding of the broader regulatory ecosystem.

- Proficiencies in data impact analysis, strategic thinking, creative problem solving, and excellent oral and written communication skills.

- Ability to evaluate the impact and drive change of key Regulatory Intelligence on disease area and project strategy.

- Ability to discern and communicate relevant Regulatory news to key collaborators and senior leaders

- Solid understanding of Regulatory Intelligence Tools.

- Experience working cross-functionally with diverse stakeholders.

- Experience working in BioPharmaceutical development including but not limited to, pharmaceutical/biotech industry and government.

Desirable Skills/Experience:

- Solid understanding of the commercial aspects of BioPharmaceutical development

- In-depth knowledge of the Respiratory & Immunology therapeutic area

- Broad background of experience working in pharmaceutical business and prior experience in leading competitive intelligence within the pharmaceutical industry or in associated industries

- Critical thinking on current global regulatory science trends and questions with a good understanding of the corresponding scientific and clinical components.

- Previous regulatory policy experience or working with external trade and scientific associations.

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That's why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that doesn't mean we're not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility. Join us in our unique and ambitious world.

Why AstraZeneca:

Here, regulatory professionals help set the pace for development by pairing rigorous science with progressive thinking. You will join a collaborative community that challenges constructively, influences external regulators, and uses data and technology to craft innovative evidence packages that achieve the strongest possible labels. We bring different disciplines together to spark bold ideas, support each other to test new approaches, and value kindness alongside ambition. Your insight will ripple across programs, moving life-changing medicines to patients faster while you grow your impact and expertise.

If you are ready to transform external signals into strategic advantage and shape the path of next-generation respiratory and immunology medicines, take the lead and make your move today.

title: Senior Data Center & AI Fabric Network Engineer - RDT Hosting and Infrastructure (HI)
description:
The Senior AI & Data Center Network Engineer is a technical expert responsible for architecting and implementing resilient, ultra-high-performance Data Center and AI/ML network infrastructures. You will lead complex projects, make critical design decisions for both traditional cloud fabrics and high-throughput GPU clusters, and leverage advanced automation to solve business challenges.


The Opportunity:

This role requires a blend of deep technical mastery in modern Spine-Leaf architectures, lossless AI fabrics, and the strategic mindset to influence vendor relationships and inter-organizational initiatives.


Key Responsibilities

As a Senior AI & DC Network Engineer, your daily contributions will balance architectural excellence with advanced engineering projects across enterprise and AI compute environments:

  • Architecture & AI Fabric Design: Lead the end-to-end design and deployment of integrated, "first-time-right" network solutions, focusing on scalable L2/L3 Spine-Leaf topologies as well as ultra-low latency, non-blocking fabrics (Rail-Optimized / Clos) tailored for AI/ML workloads.
  • NVIDIA Networking Engineering: Architect, deploy, and optimize high-speed Ethernet fabrics utilizing the NVIDIA Spectrum Ethernet Platform and NVIDIA Cumulus Linux to support high-density GPU-to-GPU communication.
  • Technical Leadership: Act as a Solution Architect for large initiatives, managing resource estimation, dependencies, and risk mitigation while leading small-to-medium technical teams across network and AI infrastructure domains.
  • Automation Engineering: Modernize operations by treating the network as code; develop and maintain Arista AVD, NVIDIA Air (for digital twin validation), Ansible, and CI/CD pipelines to ensure scalable, repeatable deployments across multi-vendor environments.
  • Technical Problem Solving & Congestion Management: Collaborate with cross-functional AI, compute, and storage teams to diagnose and resolve complex network incidents, fine-tuning lossless Ethernet parameters (RoCEv2, PFC, ECN) and performing root-cause analysis in high-stakes environments.
  • Reliability & Observability: Define and maintain Service Level Objectives (SLOs) through advanced telemetry, streaming analytics, and tools like NVIDIA NetQ to proactively monitor microbursts, tail latency, and fabric performance, maximizing "five-nines" availability.
  • Strategic Influence: Translate technical roadmaps into business value for stakeholders and steer vendor product evaluations (including next-generation high-radix switches and optics) to align with long-term organizational AI and cloud strategy.

Who You Are

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or a business field, or equivalent experience. And 5-8 years of work experience. required
  • Multi-Vendor Fabric Mastery: Deep expertise in Arista EOS and NVIDIA Cumulus Linux, with hands-on experience designing and operating NVIDIA Spectrum switches alongside traditional EVPN-VXLAN Spine-Leaf architectures and complex BGP control planes.
  • AI/ML Networking Expertise: Solid understanding of high-performance computing (HPC) and AI cluster networking requirements, including RoCEv2 (RDMA over Converged Ethernet), congestion control mechanisms (ECN, PFC, DCQCN), and high-speed optical interconnects (400G/800G).
  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Proficient in automating multi-vendor network deployments using Arista AVD, Ansible, Linux networking tools (Netplan, ifupdown2), and CI/CD pipelines (GitHub/GitLab).
  • Migration & Cutover Leadership: Experienced in leading high-stakes brownfield-to-greenfield migrations, with a focus on hitless cutovers, robust rollback planning, and zero-downtime execution.
  • Advanced Troubleshooting: Expert-level troubleshooting skills across underlay/overlay networks and Linux-based network operating systems. You exercise sound judgment and remain decisive in high-pressure, complex technical scenarios.
  • Communication & Mindset: A proactive learner who thrives in rapidly evolving AI infrastructure landscapes and translates complex system concepts into clear, actionable insights for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in a technical field preferred; CCNP (Enterprise or Service Provider), NVIDIA Networking certifications, or equivalent deep industry experience is highly desirable.

Relocation benefits are not available for this job posting.

Must be willing to work on-site in South San Francisco.

title: Internship
description:
Who are we?

Howden is a global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mindset, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 56 countries.

People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It’s what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down headhunters for years. Whatever your priorities – work / life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering – you’ll find like-minded people driving change at Howden.

Various location: Miami

Position: Broker Intern

Start date: June 2027

End date: August 2027

Pay rate: $25


What you’ll be doing


As a Broker Intern, you’ll gain hands-on exposure to the insurance brokerage industry and learn how brokers help clients identify, assess, and manage risk. You’ll work alongside experienced professionals to support client service, insurance placements, market research and account management activities while building a foundational understanding of insurance products and the client lifecycle.


In addition, you’ll also:


  • Support the preparation and coordination of client proposals, submissions, and presentations
  • Assist with market research and analyze industry trends
  • Apply classroom knowledge to real business scenarios
  • Complete administrative tasks as assigned
  • Build relationships with mentors, team members, and leaders across the organization

What are we looking for?


You'll thrive in this role if you are:


  • On track to achieve, or have achieved, a cumulative GPA of 3.2 or above
  • Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program, preferably Risk Management, Business Administration, or a related field (graduating between December 2027 and May 2028)
  • Curious, proactive, and eager to learn new concepts and skills.
  • A strong communicator who enjoys building relationships and collaborating with others.
  • Proficient with Microsoft Suite.

To be eligible for this position, you must have unrestricted authorization to work in the United States.

Why should you apply?


  • Pathway to a career at Howden: Our program is designed to identify talent for future full-time opportunities. High-performing interns may have an opportunity to pursue full-time positions following graduation.
  • Industry Exposure: You’ll have the opportunity to learn from the best in-class industry professionals and gain hands-on experience that helps you test career paths.
  • Networking: Throughout your internship, you will meet a variety of team members, senior leaders and other professionals to help support your development.
  • Entrepreneurial
  • Passionate
  • Game-changer

Our Application Process

Our application process is designed to help you show your potential, not to test what you already know!

  • Online application form: This step is designed to be quick and straightforward and shouldn't take more than 5-10 minutes to complete. At this stage, we’ll ask for key information such as your education details, eligibility to work, and a copy of your résumé.
  • Phone or video interview: You will speak to a Howden team member about the opportunity, giving you the chance to tell us more about yourself in your own time in a relaxed setting.
  • Interview Super Day: During the day, you’ll take part in interviews with colleagues from across the business, giving us the chance to learn more about your experiences, strengths, and motivations, while also giving you the opportunity to ask questions and explore whether the program is the right fit for you.

What do we offer in return?

A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:

  • Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new

  • We support each other in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges

  • We are determined to make a positive difference at work and beyond

Reasonable adjustments

We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations at Howden to ensure that our positions align well with your needs. Besides the usual adjustments such as software, IT, and office setups, we can also accommodate other changes such as flexible hours* or hybrid working*.

If you're excited by this role but have some doubts about whether it’s the right fit for you, send us your application – if your profile fits the role’s criteria, we will be in touch to assist in helping to get you set up with any reasonable adjustments you may require.

*Not all positions can accommodate changes to working hours or locations. Reach out to your Recruitment Partner if you want to know more.

title: Business Analytics Consultant Senior - Data Analytics & Visualization
description:
Position Overview

Position Overview:

At PNC, our people are our greatest differentiator and competitive advantage in the markets we serve. We are all united in delivering the best experience for our customers. We work together each day to foster an inclusive workplace culture where all of our employees feel respected, valued and have an opportunity to contribute to the company’s success. Job Description:

The Business Analytics Consultant Senior is responsible for delivering advanced analytics, Generative AI (GenAI), and Agentic AI solutions that drive strategic business outcomes and intelligent decision-making. This role partners closely with business and technology stakeholders to identify opportunities for data-driven transformation, AI-powered automation, and enhanced decision support.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical and technical expertise with hands-on experience developing AI-enabled solutions utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs), AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt engineering, and modern data platforms. This individual will help design and implement intelligent systems that augment business processes, automate complex workflows, and generate actionable insights at scale

Key Responsibilities:

• Leverage analytical tools and methodologies to provide business and technical expertise in support of data-driven decision-making.
• Partner with business stakeholders to understand business strategies, objectives, challenges, and reporting needs.
• Consult business partners to design, develop, and implement analytical solutions that address business requirements.
• Analyze large, complex datasets to identify trends, patterns, risks, and opportunities.
• Determine the most effective analytical approach and execute best practices related to solution development, validation, testing, implementation, and ongoing enhancements.
• Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards, reports, and visualizations using Power BI and other business intelligence tools.
• Perform advanced data analysis utilizing R Shiny, SQL and Python to support business initiatives and strategic projects.
• Validate data quality, accuracy, and consistency to ensure reliable reporting and insights.
• Translate analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for business partners and senior leadership.
• Present complex analytical results to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Collaborate across business, technology, and operational teams to support enterprise initiatives and business outcomes.
• Support ongoing monitoring and measurement of key performance indicators (KPIs) and business metrics.
• Document business requirements, methodologies, and analytical processes.

Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Data Science, Statistics, Information Systems, Analytics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related quantitative discipline, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
• 3+ years of experience developing data-driven solutions, analytics applications, and reporting tools in a corporate environment.
• 3+ years of experience designing, developing, and deploying advanced analytics solutions utilizing Generative AI technologies and Large Language Models (LLMs).
• Hands-on experience building AI-powered applications using Azure OpenAI Service, OpenAI APIs, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, or similar enterprise AI platforms.
• Experience developing Agentic AI solutions leveraging frameworks such as Microsoft Copilot Studio, Semantic Kernel, LangGraph, LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, or equivalent orchestration technologies.
• Strong understanding of prompt engineering, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector databases, embeddings, semantic search, and knowledge-grounding techniques.
• Experience integrating LLMs with enterprise data platforms, APIs, workflow automation tools, and business applications.
• Knowledge of Responsible AI principles, AI governance frameworks, security controls, and model evaluation methodologies.
• Strong proficiency in Python for AI/ML development, including libraries and frameworks supporting LLM applications and intelligent automation.
• Demonstrated experience performing data analysis, data reporting, and data visualization to derive actionable business insights.
• Strong understanding of data modeling, data transformation, data quality, and data governance principles.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to present complex technical concepts and analytical findings to business and executive stakeholders.
• Proven ability to collaborate effectively across technical and non-technical teams within a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience in Banking, Financial Services, Commercial Banking, Corporate Banking, or Investment Banking environments.
• Knowledge of Commercial & Investment Banking (C&IB) products, operations, risk management, client analytics, or financial reporting.
• Experience with UI/UX design principles and front-end/web application development.
• Experience building multi-agent systems that coordinate analytical workflows, reporting processes, or business operations.
• Experience with Microsoft AI technologies including Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Fabric, Copilot Studio, Power Platform AI Builder, and Microsoft 365 Copilot extensions.
• Experience implementing conversational AI, enterprise knowledge assistants, or autonomous decision-support solutions.
• Familiarity with vector databases such as Pinecone, Azure AI Search, Weaviate, Chroma, or similar technologies.
• Experience developing AI solutions within financial services, risk, compliance, fraud detection, client servicing, or commercial banking environments.

Security is fundamental to how we protect our customers, colleagues and data while enabling the Group to innovate safely and move faster.


We’re looking for an exceptional Technology Platform Lead (TPL) to lead the Chief Security Office Technology Platform. This is a high-profile leadership role combining cyber security strategy, technology transformation and large-scale engineering leadership.

The Chief Security Office provides security services across the Group, working closely with business and technology platforms to protect our customers, colleagues and data while enabling them to deliver safely and at pace.


As technology and cyber threats continue to evolve, this role will shape how we modernise and strengthen our security capabilities. You’ll build the specialist security and engineering expertise needed for the future, including security automation, AI-enabled engineering and priority cyber capabilities.


If you’re passionate about combining world-class security with engineering excellence, this is a unique opportunity to make an impact at significant scale.

You'll balance long-term investment with short-term delivery, ensuring teams remain focused on innovation, stability and customer value.

You'll bring experience leading significant engineering organisations through transformation, alongside a passion for developing people, modernising technology and delivering meaningful business outcomes.

This is a rare opportunity to lead a platform at the intersection of cyber security, engineering and business transformation.

title: Silicon Photonics Wafer Level Test Development Engineer
description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

The Role and Impact

As a Silicon Photonics Wafer Level Test Development Engineer, you will play a key role in developing advanced test solutions for Intel's silicon photonics technologies, supporting device characterization, technology development, and manufacturing readiness.

You will develop, integrate, and optimize wafer-level test methodologies, automated measurement systems, and software solutions to enable accurate, reliable, and scalable testing of silicon photonic devices.

Working closely with cross-functional teams, you will contribute to the development and deployment of advanced silicon photonics technologies while supporting Intel's silicon photonics foundry business.


Business Group

This role supports Intel's silicon photonics technology development and foundry operations, contributing to the advancement of semiconductor technologies through innovative test development, device characterization, and manufacturing solutions.


Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, implement, and optimize wafer-level test methodologies for silicon photonic devices.
  • Develop automated test solutions integrating optical and electrical instrumentation, semiconductor test equipment, hardware, and software.
  • Perform photonic device testing and characterization to evaluate device performance and identify improvement opportunities.
  • Develop software and data analysis solutions to support automated testing, measurement analysis, and performance evaluation.
  • Integrate, troubleshoot, and optimize test systems involving instrumentation, hardware, software, and measurement methods.
  • Analyze test data to identify performance trends, measurement variability, and potential device or test-related issues.
  • Collaborate with device, process, product, and manufacturing engineering teams to define test requirements and support technology development.
  • Validate and optimize test methodologies to improve measurement accuracy, repeatability, reliability, and test efficiency.
  • Support the transfer and deployment of test solutions into manufacturing environments.
  • Document measurement methods, software interfaces, and validation results to support long-term maintainability and deployment.

Behavioral Traits

The ideal candidate should demonstrate the following behavioral traits:

  • Strong analytical and technical problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication and collaboration across cross-functional engineering teams.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple technical priorities.
  • Adaptability within a dynamic technology development environment.
  • Commitment to innovation and continuous improvement.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

Candidates must possess one of the following:

  • PhD in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical discipline with 2+ years of experience in silicon photonic device testing or related test development environments.

OR

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical discipline with 4+ years of experience in one or more of the following areas:
    • Photonic device testing and characterization.
    • Data analysis using MATLAB, Python, JMP, or similar tools.
    • Optical, electrical, semiconductor, or automated test equipment and measurement systems.
    • Programming or developing data analysis solutions using C#, C++, Python, or a comparable programming language.
    • Hands-on integration or troubleshooting of systems involving instrumentation, hardware, software, and measurement methods.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience developing automated wafer-level test solutions for silicon photonic or optoelectronic devices.
  • Experience with optical and electrical wafer probing systems.
  • Experience with optical coupling, alignment, and fiber-based measurement systems.
  • Experience characterizing silicon photonic devices, including waveguides, modulators, photodetectors, or optical couplers.
  • Experience integrating optical and electrical instrumentation into automated test platforms.
  • Experience optimizing test throughput, measurement repeatability, and test system reliability.
  • Experience transferring test methodologies from research and development environments into semiconductor manufacturing.

title: Congress & HCP Engagement Strategy, Senior Manager
description:
The Opportunity

The Congress & HCP Engagement Strategy Senior Manager owns the strategic design, cross-functional orchestration, governance, and optimization of Genentech’s congress and HCP engagement strategy for assigned Therapeutic Area(s) (TAs), encompassing medical congresses and advisory boards.

Acting as the single strategic congress and advisory board engagement partner for their TA, this role evaluates clinical pipeline milestones, clinical trial readouts, and commercial brand launch priorities to define comprehensive annual engagement objectives. Working closely with Medical Affairs, Commercial Brand teams, Roche, Corporate Brand, and cross-functional leads, the role leads annual planning, sets the TA congress and ad board calendar, and defines presence recommendations, engagement formats, and investment priorities.

This is a cross-functional lead role that orchestrates the planning team to align vision, narrative and presence across multi-brand and TA-level congresses, ensuring every Congress presence is purpose-driven, appropriately structured, and positioned to deliver meaningful outcomes for Genentech and participating HCPs.

The finalized congress and engagement plan is shared with dedicated operational partners who provide the delivery layer, enabling the role to focus upstream on strategic orchestration, customer engagement design, and cross-functional alignment. This role operates within SES’s product model, partnering closely with product owners who manage standard congress products, tools, standards, and measurement, and feeding performance insights back into future congress strategy and capability development (products).


Key Responsibilities

1. Annual Planning & TA Congress Strategy

  • Lead the annual TA congress and engagement planning process in alignment with finance business cycles informing multi-year investment roadmaps and resource allocation across congresses and advisory boards.
  • Develop an integrated TA congress strategy grounded in TA objectives and priorities, customer insights, and the pipeline and product life cycle
  • Evaluate upcoming clinical trial readouts, pipeline milestones, and brand launch priorities to build a proactive annual congress plan and investment roadmap for the therapeutic area
  • Set the congress calendar for the therapy area and define the objectives and presence approach for each congress
  • Define measurable congress objectives that align with TA and brand strategy
  • Provide strategic budget stewardship across the TA portfolio, assessing investment trade-offs and aligning spend to high-impact congresses and engagement opportunities within approved budget
  • Translate standardized congress engagement products, tools and standards together with cross-functional needs, into a TA-specific congress presence scope and activation plan

2. Stakeholder Orchestration

  • Coordinate Commercial, Medical Affairs, and other functions so narrative and presence are aligned across portfolio, multi-brand, and TA-level congresses
  • Act as the primary strategic partner for Medical Affairs, Commercial, Roche and other functional leads on TA congress strategy
  • Orchestrate portfolio congress presence to optimize effectiveness and identify opportunities for efficiency across brands and functions
  • Partner closely with the Congress & Event Operations team to translate the approved strategy and activation plan into operational delivery plans, remaining engaged for strategic decisions and escalations

3. HCP Engagement & Governance

  • Define the objectives and engagement approach for congress-related HCP interactions, including purposeful 1:1 engagement, in partnership with Medical and Commercial teams and using established SES tools and processes
  • Partner with Commercial and Medical teams during annual planning to establish the strategic cadence and objectives for TA Advisory Boards, ensuring alignment with lifecycle milestones
  • Serve as the strategic escalation point for Advisory Board scope and objectives, partnering with Event Operations on delivery-related issues

4. Insights

  • Ensure TA-level congress strategy and congress-level objectives are defined and documented
  • Apply standardized measurement framework to assess congress performance against TA objectives, and communicate impact and opportunities to Medical, Commercial, and SES leadership
  • Synthesize insights across congresses to refine future congress strategy, and share structured feedback with Medical and Commercial leads and SES capability (product) leads to improve future congress engagement and standard products

5. Omnichannel Engagement Orchestration

  • Partner with relevant omnichannel teams to align congress touchpoints with broader digital customer journeys, channel plans, and follow-up strategies
  • Align the timing and sequencing of major congress activations with broader channel plans to support a cohesive HCP experience

6. Society Relationship Management & Engagement

  • Cultivate and maintain strategic relationships with key medical and scientific societies relevant to the TA (e.g., ASCO, ASH, AAN, AAO) to inform long-term engagement and sponsorship approaches.
  • Use established measures to assess congress and society engagement effectiveness and apply learnings to future strategy and investment decisions

Who You Are

  • 9+ years of experience in pharmaceuticals or related industry
  • 5+ years experience in congress or event strategy, partnering with brand and medical teams
  • Bachelor’s degree required (life sciences, business administration, etc.)
  • Strong scientific fluency and business acumen, with the proven ability to quickly learn complex disease states and translate clinical pipeline data into engagement strategies
  • Experience setting strategy for major medical congresses (e.g., ASCO, ASH, AAN, AAO, etc.)
  • Strong command of HCP engagement compliance, process and governance frameworks (Congresses & Ad Boards)Proven stakeholder management and strategic planning skills in cross-functional environments
  • Experience supporting global or national therapy-area congress strategies
  • Willingness and ability to travel as needed, up to 30%.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Therapeutic area experience in Oncology, Hematology, Immunology, Neurology, Ophthalmology, or CVRM/Metabolism
  • Familiarity with omnichannel engagement and end-to-end HCP journey design
  • Experience working within a product operating model, partnering with product or capability owners and agile teams

Location

  • This role is based in South San Francisco and offers a hybrid schedule working 3 day per week on campus
  • Relocation benefits are NOT available on this posting

We are hiring for multiple roles/openings on this posting.


The expected salary range for this position based on the primary location of South San Francisco, CA is $137,900/yr to $256,100/yr. Job Description

Position Summary:
The Ontario Structured Psychotherapy (OSP) program aims to increase access to publicly funded evidence-based Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) and related approaches for Ontarians with depression anxiety and anxiety-related conditions. The Ontario Structured Psychotherapy West Region (OSP West) program is jointly operated by St. Joseph’s Healthcare Hamilton (SJHH) and St. Joseph’s Health Care London. For this position the applicant will be employed by SJHH and will be expected to support centralized screening intake triage and referral management for the OSP program across the entire Ontario West region.

The OSP Intake Worker will work in collaboration with the OSP West centralized intake team and be responsible for various screening intake triage and referral management processes including: reviewing and triaging referrals for suitability for OSP (including reviewing and interpreting clinical measures) liaising with referral sources to obtain additional information when needed conducting risk assessments and safety planning as clinically indicated obtaining consent for participation in OSP completing brief telephone intake and triage interviews clinical documentation basic counselling to distressed caller basic system navigation and providing support to clinicians completing intake assessments. This is a hybrid role that provides an opportunity to work both virtually and on-site. On-site requirements will be determined based on the needs of the service and location of the applicant’s residence.

SJHH and the OSP West program are committed to hiring individuals who represent the diversity of the population we serve. We strongly encourage applications from qualified candidates from all cultures Indigenous Black and racialized communities people with lived experience of mental health and/or addictions challenges people with diverse sexual and gender identities people living with disabilities and neurodivergent people. SJHH and the OSP West program strive for a diverse inclusive accessible and equitable workplace where all employees and volunteers feel valued and respected. As such it is critical that applicants possess a strong understanding of client-centered anti-racist anti-oppressive practice.

Qualifications:
•Undergraduate degree in Clinical or Counselling Psychology Social Work Occupational Therapy or related health discipline.
• Registered member and in good standing with relevant professional college/regulatory body (e.g. Ontario College of Social Workers and Social Service Workers)
•Position requires a minimum of 1-2 years previous experience working in the mental health field including:
•Demonstrated knowledge and practiced skills in providing culturally safe and responsive mental health services to clients of diverse ethno-racial and cultural backgrounds is preferred.
•Experience working in a community-based or outpatient setting.

Other Knowledge Skills and Competencies:
•Experience with screening intake triage and referral management processes in a mental health setting.
•Experience conducting risk assessments safety planning and crisis intervention.
•Experience conducting brief intake assessments in person and by telephone.
•Familiarity with clinical self-report screener measures (e.g. PHQ-9 GAD-7 etc.).
•Knowledge of diagnostic categories and criteria as listed in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5) specifically those related to depression anxiety and anxiety-related conditions.
•Basic knowledge of structured psychotherapy treatment modalities utilized with the OSP program (e.g. Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) etc.).
•Familiarity with a stepped-care clinical model.
•Knowledge of local and provincial mental health and addictions programs/services and experience providing service navigation based on client need and program availability.
•Demonstrated knowledge of relevant sections of legislation e.g. Mental Health Act Personal Health Information Protection Act Regulated Health Professions Act Health Care Consent Act and professional standards to ensure compliance and consistency in provision of client care.
•Knowledge of emergency client care procedures as taught in Emergency First Response Crisis Intervention and fire procedures to promote coordinated and consistent practices in response to emergency events i.e. Code Blue; Code White Code Red.
•Knowledge of program and hospital policies and procedures in order to practice within the expected standards of the organization and to recognize abnormal events that may affect client care activities or safety and need to be reported to a manager in order to provide a safe environment for client and staff.
•Demonstrated knowledge and comfort with computer software to generate correspondence and input data for a variety of facility-wide tools e.g. Microsoft Office Suite electronic health records.
•Excellent verbal and written communication skills to effectively communicate with clients family members referral sources the OSP West team and wider OSP network.
•Strong interpersonal skills to develop and maintain strong working relationships with clients family members referral sources community partners and OSP West clinicians managers consultants and partners.
•Time management and organizational skills to effectively address and prioritize multiple tasks and timelines in a fast-paced environment.
•Attention to detail in collecting and documenting client and program information.
•Experience and comfort in providing services virtually and/or by telephone.
•Ability to work with clients from diverse ethno-racial and cultural backgrounds.
•Passionate about contributing to positive social change and commitment to anti-oppression and anti-racism to reduce health disparities and promote health equity.
•Fluency in French and/or proficiency in a second language is considered an asset.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
•Receive and transcribe email fax and phone referrals into the e-referral system.
•Review incoming referrals from primary care providers (PCPs) other healthcare/non-healthcare providers and self-referrals for completeness and initial suitability for OSP based on standardized eligibility criteria.
•Contact PCPs other healthcare/non-healthcare providers or client if further information/clarification is required to determine initial suitability for OSP.
•Consult with OSP Intake Clinician and/or other team members if initial eligibility is unclear.
•Ensure appropriate client consent(s) are received/complete (e.g. consent to email/leave voicemail etc.).
•Distribute client intake questionnaires (including clinical measures) and monitor/follow-up for completion.
•Review intake questionnaires and clinical measures for completion and suitability for OSP; note potential safety risks related to clinical measures (e.g. item 9 on PHQ-9) for follow-up.
•Input completed clinical measures into measurement-based care tool.
•Contribute to service navigation resource development and provide basic service navigation for clients deemed not suitable for OSP; communicate non-OSP service recommendations to referral source and/or client.
•Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation of referral information and referral status as referral progresses through the screening triage and intake process.
•Provide basic counselling to distressed caller – provide reassurance support and validation
•Maintain confidentiality and release of information in accordance with hospital policies and provincial legislation.
•Actively incorporate anti-racist anti-oppressive practices and principles at all levels of care.
•Based on provided referral information (clinical documentation and clinical measure scores) identify clients who may be at increased risk of suicidality self-harm behaviours or homicide.
•Conduct risk assessments and safety planning as clinically indicated and document in the clinical chart.
•Provide information about emergency and crisis resources to clients as indicated.
•Triage referral appropriately based on urgency either for treatment within the OSP program further assessment within the OSP program (if appropriate) or connection to other community resources (e.g. crisis services).
•Maintain communication related to risk assessment and safety planning with OSP West team and other relevant healthcare providers (e.g. referral source) with client consent.
•Consult with other clinicians (intake clinicians clinical consultants clinical network lead) as needed throughout the risk assessment and safety planning process.
•Complete brief telephone intake and triage interview with client to review completed measures (if required) provide information about OSP obtain additional information about presenting problem and suitability conduct risk assessment and safety planning (as indicated) and discuss next steps (e.g. treatment plan additional assessment service navigation etc.).
•Schedule in-depth Clinical Intake and Triage Assessment (“intake assessment”) appointment with OSP Intake Clinician for clients who require additional assessment after telephone intake and triage interview.
•Communicate scheduled appointment details to client referral source and OSP Intake Clinician.
•Review and email additional clinical measures client information sheet and client consent required for completion prior to intake assessment; ensure completed documents are provided to OSP Intake Clinician.
•Maintain accurate and timely documentation related to brief telephone intake interview and scheduling.
•Support administrative assistants in receiving/responding to incoming telephone calls and emails related to the OSP West program namely those that require clinical knowledge/expertise.
•Assist the Program Manager and Network Clinical Lead on specific OSP-related projects related to the regional development of the OSP program as required.

Oracle Techno-Functional Engineer – Finance Platforms

The role focuses on improving transaction processing, accounting accuracy, integrations, reporting, and financial close activities.

description: Uddevalla – en plats för hela livet Välkommen att bli en del av vår växande kommun - och att tillsammans med oss arbeta för att ge våra kommuninvånare ännu bättre service. Du är lyhörd och kommunkatiov och bidrar till teamets och arbetsplatsens utveckling.Vi lägger stor vikt vid personlig kompetens, engagemang och din fallenhet för uppdraget.KvalifikationerVi söker dig som:    Har en akademisk examen inom datateknik, systemvetenskap eller erfarenhet som arbetsgivaren bedömer likvärdig. Har erfarenhet av Git och GitHub samt av att driftsätta lösningar med Docker i lokala servermiljöer.    Har erfarenhet att arbeta med SQL-databaser och databasdesign.    Har erfarenhet och känner dig trygg med att arbeta med programmeringsspråken Python och TypeScript.    Har erfarenhet av AI samt att integrera AI-funktionalitet i utvecklade lösningar.    Kan använda AI som assistans för kodning samt för att effektivera utvecklingsprocessen.MeriterandeErfarenhet av ledarskap och att leda team med hjälp av exempelvis KanbanHar erfarenhet av att utveckla lösningar som uppfyller krav på digital tillgänglighet, dataskydd och informationssäkerhet i offentlig sektorÖvrigtIntervjuer kommer att ske löpande så vänta inte med din ansökan!
