title: Vice President, Lending Operations
description:
About Our Company


We’re a diversified financial services leader with more than $1.5 trillion in assets under management, administration and advisement as of year-end 2024. Our team of 22,000 people across 19 countries, serves more than 3.5 million individual, small business and institutional clients. We are a longstanding leader in financial planning and advice, a global asset manager and an insurer. Our unwavering focus on our clients and strong financial foundation connects each of our unique businesses – Ameriprise Financial, Columbia Threadneedle Investments and RiverSource Insurance and Annuities. Here, we foster meaningful careers, invest in the future, and make a difference for clients, institutions and communities around the world.

Job Description

This is an opportunity to shape the next chapter of lending operations within our Clearing Broker-Dealer and expand your enterprise impact at Ameriprise. You will lead Margin, Pledge Lending, and Securities Lending operations while strengthening credit risk governance, modernizing processes, and enabling responsible growth. The role offers broad influence across Ameriprise Bank, Products, Trading, Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Technology. You will also build and develop a high-performing team equipped to support the evolving needs of our clearing and wealth management businesses.

Responsibilities

Set the strategy, governance, operating model, and priorities for Margin, Pledge Lending, and Securities Lending operations to deliver strong client outcomes and support responsible business growth.


Own the operational credit risk and control framework, including margin requirements, extensions of credit, concentrations, large-loan exposure, exceptions, and escalation protocols.


Establish and maintain effective policies, controls, risk tolerances, and governance standards for the firm’s broker-dealer lending activities.


Lead modernization, automation, and scalable process improvements that increase efficiency, strengthen controls, enhance service, and support growth.


Monitor regulatory and industry developments and partner with Risk, Compliance, Legal, Product, Trading, Technology, and Ameriprise Bank to ensure operational readiness and effective implementation.


Provide decisive leadership during significant operational, credit, regulatory, technology, and client issues, ensuring clear communication, effective mitigation, and timely resolution.


Develop performance, exposure, and risk metrics that give senior leaders clear insight into results, emerging risks, and opportunities.


Build a high-performing organization through coaching, talent development, succession planning, engagement, and performance management.


Qualifications

10+ years of relevant financial services experience, including significant experience in broker-dealer operations, lending, credit, or related operational and control functions.


Demonstrated leadership experience building organizational capability, developing talent, managing performance, and leading teams through change.


Deep knowledge of broker-dealer operations and the regulatory requirements governing margins and extensions of credit.


Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.


Active Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) Series 7 and Series 24 registrations.


Knowledge of FINRA, Federal Reserve, and U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission requirements applicable to broker-dealer margin and credit activities; experience with credit risk governance programs is preferred.


Experience developing financial, regulatory, risk, and management reporting; an advanced degree or relevant professional designation is preferred.


Strong strategic leadership, communication, influencing, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and critical issues.

title: Senior Innovation Engineer
description:
At Dow, we believe in putting people first and we’re passionate about delivering integrity, respect and safety to our customers, our employees and the planet.

Our people are at the heart of our solutions. They reflect the communities we live in and the world where we do business. Their diversity is our strength. We’re a community of relentless problem solvers that offers the daily opportunity to contribute with your perspective, transform industries and shape the future. Our purpose is simple - to deliver a sustainable future for the world through science and collaboration. If you’re looking for a challenge and meaningful role, you’re in the right place.

About you and this role


Dow has an exciting opportunity for a Senior Innovation Engineer located in Elizabethtown, KY! You will champion continuous improvement through existing assets, develops value cases, and implements expense and capital solutions to expose true value. You will partner across the area business engineer, supply chain, and technology center to optimize plant assets, product mix, and improvement concepts. You will own financial acumen and value creation for the area, scale-up timing, and the strategic improvement plan, validating concepts before business discussion. You will provide critical subject-matter input for the technology roadmap and mentors the area business engineer and performance engineer in value case creation.

Responsibilities

  • Own financial acumen and value creation for the area in partnership with the finance manager
  • Partner with the area business engineer and supply chain on value creation through asset and product mix optimization
  • Validate improvement concepts using both capital and non-capital solutions, focusing on exposing true value
  • Apply continuous improvement methodology to determine ways to close production gaps
  • Provide critical subject-matter input for the area technology roadmap in partnership with the technology center
  • Support innovation activities including scale-ups and process research and development
  • Own and execute scale-up timing for the plant
  • Set and execute the strategic improvement plan for the area, validating concepts
  • Work with quality and performance engineers to close gaps in product capability and stability
  • Identify, prioritize, and implement improvement opportunities aligned with plant, global technology, and business objectives



Required Qualifications

  • A minimum of a Bachelor's degree in Engineering OR relevant military experience at or above a U.S. E5 ranking OR Canadian Petty Officer 2nd Class ranking is required.
  • A minimum of 3 years of experience in plant-based or project-based roles.
  • Must be capable to execute small and large capital and expense projects.
  • A minimum requirement for this U.S. based position is the ability to work legally in the United States. No visa sponsorship/support is available for this position, including for any type of U.S. permanent residency (green card).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Requires prior experience in plant-based roles such as performance engineer

Your Skills


  • Manufacturing Processes: Deep understanding of how equipment, materials, and unit operations interact to produce products safely, efficiently, and at consistent quality.
  • Collaborative Spirit: Effectively partners with operations, maintenance, technology, and EH&S to solve problems and implement sustainable improvements. Builds trust and alignment across teams.
  • Production Engineering: Applies advanced technical expertise to optimize plant operations, resolve complex production issues, and support safe, reliable, and cost‑effective manufacturing.
  • Plant & Process Safety: Reinforces safe work practices and operating discipline through strong field presence and sound daily decision‑making, while ensuring process safety risks are identified, understood, and controlled through effective application of standards and management systems.
  • Process Improvements: Identifies performance gaps and leads data‑driven improvements that enhance efficiency, reliability, and cost while aligning with business priorities.
  • Lean Manufacturing: Applies lean principles to eliminate waste, improve flow, and increase productivity without compromising safety or quality.
  • Proactive Problem Solving: Anticipates issues by monitoring trends, alarms, and KPIs, and leads root cause analysis to prevent recurrence.
  • Data Analysis: Uses process data and performance metrics to guide troubleshooting, operational decisions, and continuous improvement efforts.
  • High Reliability: Promotes consistent and predictable plant performance by reinforcing operating discipline, understanding failure modes, and addressing reliability risks early.

Physical Requirements

Willing and able to meet the physical demands of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Wear safety equipment, such as earplugs, gloves, safety-toe shoes, helmets and safety glasses.
  • Stand or walk for extended periods of time.

Additional Notes


Relocation assistance is not available for this position.

Dow invests in total rewards programs to help you manage all aspects of you: your pay, your health, your life, your future, and your career. You bring your background, talent, and perspective to work every day. Dow rewards that commitment by investing in your total wellbeing.

title: Emergency Department Tech (ERT), PRN
description:
BASIC PURPOSE OF THE JOB

An employee who performs tasks which involve specific nursing care for patients delegated by and performed under the direction of a Registered Professional Nurse.

REPORTS TO

  • Nurse Manager

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Supervisory Responsibilities: YES

Minimum Education: High School Diploma/GED

Degree: General

License/Certification Required: BLS required.

Minimum Work Experience: 6 months experience or training required. Nursing assistant, orderly or EMT experience preferred.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Demonstrates effective communication and service excellence skills.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Safely and efficiently transfers patients to and/or from other patient care areas as directed, including patients on oxygen and/or IV therapy.
  • Consistently adheres to safe Infection Control practices.
  • Collects specimens (throat, NP, urine, stool and sputum), labels them accurately and ensures they are sent to lab.
  • Performs patient care procedures as ordered by the RN or MD.
  • Assists with patient care needs and supplies, personal care needs and nourishments.
  • Correctly applies splints and traction as needed; performs crutch fitting and instructs patients/families in crutch walking.
  • Performs correct wound cleaning and dressing under nursing supervision.
  • Assists with examination procedures or treatments. May have access to minimal risk medications.
  • Maintains cleanliness and stock of both clinical and non-clinical areas.
  • Accurately collects patient data under the supervision of the RN.
  • Demonstrates critical thinking and prioritization while placing patients in rooms.
  • Demonstrates professional and effective communication among co-workers and interacts with all patients, staff, volunteers, etc. in a considerate, helpful, and courteous manner, as observed by management observation and peer input.
  • Instructs and assists families in a kind and courteous manner and assists other team members as requested within scope of practice and hospital policy.
  • Fosters mature professional relationships with fellow employees in a courteous, friendly, manner as measured by management observation and peer input.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS-Note: Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

  • Heavy lifting, pushing, and pulling is required up to 50 lbs occasionally, 20-30 lbs frequently, and 10lbs constantly to move objects of up to 150 lbs. Sudden emergency situations have the potential for exposure to lifting or moving of up to 150 lbs. Frequent bending, walking, sitting squatting, reaching, and standing are required. Keyboard/computer use and/or repetitive motions may be required.

title: CRA2
description:
CRA2

Syneos Health® is a leading fully-integrated life sciences services organization built to accelerate customer success. We partner with innovators at every point across the drug development and commercialization continuum, helping them navigate complexity, anticipate change and accelerate progress.

Our Clinical Solutions team members act with a drug development mindset, applying their years of experience and deep expertise to truly understand customer needs and represent those in the solutions we shape.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to deliver – for one another, our customers, and, most importantly, for those in need.

Discover what your 25,000 future colleagues already know:

Why Syneos Health
• We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
• We are committed to building an inclusive culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Central to this is our purpose – Driven to Deliver – which captures the passion of our colleagues to show up each day and shape solutions that have the ability to dramatically impact someone’s life.
• We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because we know that when we bring together smart colleagues from across the world, we can shape the future of healthcare, driving impact for customers and defining the pace of patient progress.

Job Responsibilities

  • Performs site qualification, site initiation, interim monitoring, site management activities and close-out visits (performed on-site or remotely) ensuring regulatory, ICH-GCP and/or Good Pharmacoepidemiology Practice (GPP) and protocol compliance. Uses judgment and experience to evaluate overall performance of site and site staff and to provide recommendations regarding site-specific actions; immediately communicates/escalates serious issues to the project team and develops action plans. Maintains a working knowledge of ICH/GCP Guidelines or other applicable guidance, relevant regulations, and company SOPs/processes.
  • Verifies the process of obtaining informed consent has been adequately performed and documented for each subject/patient, as required/appropriate. Demonstrates diligence in protecting the confidentiality of each subject/patient. Assesses factors that might affect subject/patient’s safety and clinical data integrity at an investigator/physician site such as protocol deviation/violations and pharmacovigilance issues.
  • Per the Clinical Monitoring/Site Management Plan (CMP/SMP): Assesses site processes. Conducts Source Document Review of appropriate site source documents and medical records. Verifies required clinical data entered in the case report form (CRF) is accurate and complete. Applies query resolution techniques remotely and on site, and provides guidance to site staff as necessary, driving query resolution to closure within agreed timelines. Utilizes available hardware and software to support the effective conduct of the clinical study data review and capture. Verifies site compliance with electronic data capture requirements.
  • May perform investigational product (IP) inventory, reconciliation and reviews storage and security. Verifies the IP has been dispensed and administered to subjects/patients according to the protocol. Verifies issues or risks associated with blinded or randomized information related to IP. Applies knowledge of GCP/local regulations and organizational procedures to ensure IP is appropriately (re)labelled, imported and released/returned.
  • Routinely reviews the Investigator Site File (ISF) for accuracy, timeliness and completeness. Reconciles contents of the ISF with the Trial Master File (TMF). Ensures the investigator/physician site is aware of the requirement of archiving essential documents in accordance with local guidelines and regulations.
  • Documents activities via confirmation letters, follow-up letters, trip reports, communication logs, and other required project documents as per SOPs and Clinical Monitoring Plan/Site Management Plan. Supports subject/patient recruitment, retention and awareness strategies. Enters data into tracking systems as required to track all observations, ongoing status and assigned action items to resolution.
  • For assigned activities, understands project scope, budgets, and timelines; manages site-level activities / communication to ensure project objectives, deliverables and timelines are met. Must be able to quickly adapt to changing priorities to achieve goals / targets.
  • May act as primary liaison with study site personnel, or in collaboration with Central Monitoring Associate. Ensures all assigned sites and project-specific site team members are trained and compliant with applicable requirements
  • Prepares for and attends Investigator Meetings and/or sponsor face to face meetings. Participates in global clinical monitoring/project staff meetings (inclusive of Sponsor representation, as applicable) and attends clinical training sessions according to the project specific requirements.
  • Provides guidance at the site and project level towards audit readiness standards and supports preparation for audit and required follow-up actions.
  • Maintains a working knowledge of ICH/GCP Guidelines or other applicable guidance, relevant regulations, and company SOPs/processes; completes assigned training as required. For Real World Late Phase, the CRA II will use the business card title of Site Management Associate II. Additional responsibilities include:Site support throughout the study lifecycle from site identification through close-out. Knowledge of local requirements for real world late phase study designs.Chart abstraction activities and data collection
    Collaboration with Sponsor affiliates, medical science liaisons and local country staff. The SMA II may be requested to train junior staff. Identify and communicate out of scope activities to Lead CRA/Project Manager. Proactively suggest potential sites based on local knowledge of treatment patterns, patient advocacy and Health Care Provider (HCP) associations.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or RN in a related field or equivalent combination of education, training and experience
  • Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice/ICH Guidelines and other applicable regulatory requirements
  • Must demonstrate good computer skills and be able to embrace new technologies
  • Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to manage required travel of up to 75% on a regular basis
  • US ONLY: As part of your employment with Syneos Health, you may be deployed to Sites that require certain medical and other personal information to gain facility access. Pursuant to our Employee Privacy Notice, Syneos Health can provide the Sites with the information necessary for you to gain such access. Further, a Site may ask you for additional information beyond that which Syneos Health has in its possession. You are required to comply with any such Site requests as a condition of your employment with Syneos Health. Please note that failure to provide requested information may result in a Site barring you from entry, which could put your ongoing employment at risk.

Get to know Syneos Health


Over the past 5 years, we have worked with 94% of all Novel FDA Approved Drugs, 95% of EMA Authorized Products and over 200 Studies across 73,000 Sites and 675,000+ Trial patients.

No matter what your role is, you’ll take the initiative and challenge the status quo with us in a highly competitive and ever-changing environment. Learn more about Syneos Health.

description:

Under limited supervision, designs, develops, tests, debugs and deploys complex customer-intent software solutions, along with creating and supporting software tools and utilities required for the operation, maintenance, and control of the software system. Makes complex modifications to existing software to fit specialized needs and configurations and maintains program libraries and technical documentation. Essential Duties and responsibilities

title: Scientist, Discovery
description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

Job Description

The Scientist, Discovery conducts hands-on early discovery research within the Tumor Intrinsic Biology group in Research Oncology. This role investigates molecular mechanisms that influence cancer cell identity, tumor maintenance, and therapeutic response; applies molecular, cellular, functional genomics, and quantitative approaches to evaluate therapeutic hypotheses; and develops experimental assays and techniques relevant to emerging therapeutic modalities. This role will collaborate closely with colleagues across oncology biology, chemistry, structural biology, translational medicine, and computational sciences to develop novel therapeutic hypotheses and advance early discovery programs.

This is a fully onsite position based in Foster City, CA.

As a Scientist, Discovery at Gilead, you will...

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, execute, and interpret experiments investigating transcriptional regulation, cell-state and lineage control, oncogenic signaling, and cancer dependencies.
  • Develop and apply molecular and cellular assays and relevant ex vivo and in vivo models to generate mechanistic insights into cancer biology and therapeutic response.
  • Contribute to target identification and validation, mechanism-of-action studies, and the evaluation of therapeutic hypotheses within early discovery oncology programs.
  • Apply quantitative and mechanistic approaches to connect molecular perturbations with cellular phenotypes and tumor vulnerabilities.
  • Analyze and integrate experimental data to identify scientific questions and propose next experiments within assigned projects.
  • Establish and apply functional and cell-based assays to characterize molecules, biological pathways, mechanisms of action, and therapeutic response.
  • Develop experimental assays and techniques related to induced proximity, targeted protein degradation, and transcription-factor localization, mobility, and dynamics.
  • Adapt experimental approaches based on emerging data, scientific findings, and project needs.
  • Collaborate with colleagues across oncology biology, chemistry, screening, and other scientific functions.
  • Communicate scientific findings and recommendations through presentations, written reports, and cross-functional discussions.

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor’s Degree and 6+ years of experience

OR

Master’s Degree and 4+ years of experience

OR

PhD or PharmD and 0+ years of experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Scientific background in oncogenic signaling, transcriptional regulation, cancer cell plasticity, lineage control, and/or tumor dependencies.
  • Hands-on expertise in mammalian cell culture and molecular and cellular biology techniques, including flow cytometry, imaging, and genetic-perturbation approaches such as CRISPR-based methods.
  • Experience with functional genomics and transcriptomic approaches, including genetic screens, bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, and/or chromatin-profiling approaches such as ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, or CUT&Tag.
  • Experience with quantitative live-cell imaging and/or approaches for studying transcription-factor localization, mobility, and dynamics.
  • Experience developing and applying assays to investigate pathway biology, target dependency, mechanism of action, or therapeutic response.
  • Experience with emerging therapeutic modalities, such as induced-proximity approaches, targeted protein degradation, or molecular glues.
  • Experience with complex ex vivo systems and/or in vivo tumor models.
  • Experience evaluating diverse therapeutic modalities in a drug-discovery setting.
  • Postdoctoral research experience is preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently plan and conduct bench research, critically evaluate data, troubleshoot complex experimental challenges, and formulate testable hypotheses.
  • Ability to learn and apply different scientific techniques, adapt experimental plans based on data, and work across multiple areas of biology.
  • Ability to think beyond an immediate experiment and develop a logical sequence of studies toward project-level proof of concept.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in collaborative, multidisciplinary research environments.
  • Clear scientific communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Scientific curiosity, creativity, adaptability, and commitment to rigorous, quantitative, and reproducible research.

People Leader Accountabilities:

  • Create Inclusion - knowing the business value of diverse teams, modeling inclusion, and embedding the value of diversity in the way they manage their teams.
  • Develop Talent - understand the skills, experience, aspirations and potential of their employees and coach them on current performance and future potential. They ensure employees are receiving the feedback and insight needed to grow, develop and realize their purpose.
  • Empower Teams - connect the team to the organization by aligning goals, purpose, and organizational objectives, and holding them to account. They provide the support needed to remove barriers and connect their team to the broader ecosystem.

title: Software Engineer, Database Systems — Database.com / Hyper
description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

What You'll Be Doing & Why It Matters

We’re hiring systems and database engineers across experience levels to build Database.com and advance Hyper, Salesforce’s database engine for interactive query processing.

Hyper powers analytics in Tableau and query processing in Salesforce Data 360. With Database.com, we’re building on that foundation to give developers and AI agents direct access to a database for application data, transactions, analytics, and retrieval across cloud and local environments.

Depending on your interests and experience, you’ll contribute to areas such as:

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Query optimization, query compilation, code generation, and parallel execution.
  • Storage engines, indexing, caching, compression, and efficient I/O.
  • Transactions, concurrency control, recovery, and concurrent read/write workloads.
  • Streaming ingestion, lakehouse writes, compaction, and open formats such as Apache Iceberg and Parquet as well as internal optimized storage formats.
  • Distributed systems, federated query processing, and serverless scheduling and resource isolation.
  • Local and embedded database execution, including WebAssembly.



Minimum Requirements

  • Systems programming experience in C++, Rust, or a comparable language, and a willingness to work extensively in C++.
  • A solid understanding of data structures, algorithms, memory management, and concurrency.
  • Experience in one or more relevant areas: databases, compilers, operating systems, storage, distributed systems, networking, or performance engineering.
  • Strong product judgment and the ability to turn customer needs into clear priorities, practical requirements, and useful capabilities.
  • An ability to turn a difficult problem into a testable hypothesis and use measurements to guide implementation.
  • Clear technical communication and care in reviewing other people’s work.
  • Degree or equivalent relevant experience required. Experience will be evaluated based on the core competencies for the role (e.g. extracurricular leadership roles, military experience, volunteer roles, work experience, etc.)



Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with LLVM, assembly, SIMD, modern CPU architectures, asynchronous I/O, or cloud storage would be useful.
  • So would work on SQL semantics, query optimizers, transaction processing, or reproducible systems benchmarks.
  • We expect candidates to bring strengths in some of these areas and develop others on the team.



You’ll contribute throughout design, implementation, testing, performance evaluation, and production use. That includes reading unfamiliar code, investigating regressions, explaining tradeoffs, and using real workloads to decide what to improve. We care about correctness, predictable latency, throughput, and resource efficiency.

Engineers on this team are also expected to take on product responsibilities. You’ll work with users to understand their needs and identify the problems worth solving. You’ll maintain a strong overview of database and systems research, competing products, and industry developments, and use that knowledge to guide product decisions. You’ll shape requirements, set priorities, make scope and delivery tradeoffs, and use feedback and usage data to evaluate results. We expect you to relentlessly drive the product forward, turning ideas into shipped capabilities and following through until they solve the intended problem.

We expect every engineer to be an effective manager of AI agents. You’ll translate product goals into well-defined tasks, delegate substantial engineering work to agents, coordinate parallel efforts, and review and integrate their results. Managing agents is a core engineering responsibility on this team. You’ll be expected to continually improve these workflows to deliver faster and more efficiently, while owning the technical decisions and the quality of what ships.

Scope and ownership will reflect your experience. Early-career candidates can demonstrate their abilities through coursework, research, internships, open-source contributions, or substantial independent projects. For senior candidates, we look for experience delivering complex systems and guiding technical and product decisions.

We’re looking for engineers with:

Familiarity with database internals is valuable; engineers from adjacent systems fields are also welcome.

Hyper began as a database research project at the Technical University of Munich. The team continues to combine original systems work with the demands of a production database. You’ll have the opportunity to develop new techniques, examine their behavior in detail, and ship them to users.

title: Deputy Court Clerk III
description:
Job Description Summary

This position is an intermediate level clerical classification performing moderately difficult tasks under a moderate level of supervision. Assigned tasks typically center upon a particular business processes related to the processing of appeals. The primary functions include the processing of all incoming appeals received from lower courts, as well as all appeals from the Superior Court to the Court of Appeals and Supreme Court. The specialist position requires a higher level of learning and more responsibility within the unit.


This classification is distinguished from all other clerical classifications by the specialized nature of the moderately complex tasks assigned. This classification requires knowledge of all appeal support tasks and being able to complete specialized tasks focused upon the processing of appeals

Job Description

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

· Inputs data into a computer system.

· Receives, categorizes, and processes legal documents and exhibits.

· Insures that all appeals received are processed timely pursuant to statutes.

· Interacts directly with the public both on the phone and in person.

· Performs specialized clerical tasks with a moderate level of difficulty in support of specific appeal processes.

· Must be able to maintain a high level of confidentiality in all work-related activities.

· Must be able to operate various pieces of office equipment.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

Knowledge of:

· English composition, grammar, punctuation, and spelling.

· Office practices and procedures.

· Basic computer skills.

· Keyboarding experience.

· Automated information systems.

· Legal terminology and legal forms preferred.

· Court proceedings preferred.

Skill in:

Customer Service (i.e., the ability to effectively, politely, calmly and professionally interact with the public in problematic situations, as well as with other court personnel and other jurisdictions.

Ability to:

· Effectively handle and prioritize multiple tasks and inquiries.

· Identify, organize, and sort legal paperwork and exhibits.

· Organize effectively.

· Follow brief oral and written instructions quickly and accurately.

· Operate or learn a variety of office machines.

· Research and verify completeness and accuracy of specific information.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

This lateral or promotional opportunity is open to all Clerk of Court employees, regardless of length of service.

· A high school diploma or equivalent is required

· Completed coursework in legal terminology, legal office procedures or other related legal functions and one year of legal clerical experience involving the preparation and processing of legal documents or providing legal clerical support in a court setting or to an attorney.

Applicable/relevant Clerk of the Court experience may be substituted for the aforementioned coursework preference.

LICENSES AND CERTIFICATES

None required.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS/WORKING CONDITIONS

Typically performs duties in an office environment. Lifting of 25 to 35 lbs. is required in some assignments.

DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS

This is a court classified position that reports to the Criminal Deputy Court Clerk Supervisor. This position performs duties under direct supervision

title: HR Benefits Specialist
description:
Job Summary

The HR Benefits Specialist is responsible for overseeing all aspects of employee benefits administration, ensuring compliance with applicable state and federal regulations, and optimizing benefits processes for efficiency and employee satisfaction. This role involves direct engagement with employees, HR partners, and external vendors to manage benefits enrollment, resolve complex claims, and promote awareness of available programs.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Manages all functions related to employee benefits, including health, dental, vision, short-term and long-term disability insurance, workers' compensation claims, flexible spending account plans, and the Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

  • Monitors benefit elections, reviews arrears reports, and ensures accurate processing of salary and benefits changes. Engages with the DMBA to maintain and update benefits information.
  • Identifies opportunities to enhance benefits processes, improve efficiency, and strengthen customer service.
  • Reviews Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) change reports to ensure correct premium adjustments.
  • Provides customer service and advocates for employees in resolving complex benefits claims, eligibility, and coverage issues. Acts as a liaison between employees and benefit vendors.
  • Works closely with HR partners, employees, and external vendors to manage benefits-related concerns and promote awareness of available programs.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualification and Experience Requirements

  • A bachelor's degree in human resources, business administration, or related field.
  • Three years of professional level experience in employee benefits or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
  • Demonstrated customer service and presentation skills.
  • Proficient with MS-Suite of products and Workday.

Skills

  • Strong knowledge of employee benefits administration, compliance, and reporting.
  • Experience with HR software systems, including Workday and PeopleSoft preferred.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and customer service skills.
  • Ability to analyze benefits data, generate reports, and identify trends.
  • Strong problem-solving and organizational skills.

Air-conditioned office environment with minimal physical effort required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

title: Director, Trust Operations
description:
The Director, Trust Operations provides leadership and subject matter expertise across trust, custody, and investment operations supporting retirement plan products. John Hancock Trust Company acts as directed trustee or custodian for retirement clients using John Hancock Retirement Plan Services.


The successful candidate brings strong custody knowledge, experience with separately managed accounts, an understanding of unitization fundamentals, and the communication skills to explain complex operational topics clearly and confidently.


Position Responsibilities:

  • Lead trust and custody operations, including trading support, unitized fund servicing, reconciliation, nightly pricing and statement reporting.
  • Provide expertise in custody and sub-custody models, separately managed accounts, complex retirement investments and unitization fundamentals.
  • Manage trust agreements, amendments, required filings, client inquiries and day-to-day trust matters accurately and timely.
  • Maintain policies and procedures, train staff, strengthen coverage and identify control improvements.
  • Identify operational, fiduciary, regulatory, technology and third-party risks and drive sustainable corrective actions.
  • Optimize processes through simplification, standardization, automation and root-cause analysis.
  • Partner with Sales and Service on client meetings, RFPs, due diligence, finalist presentations and operational reviews.
  • Work effectively within Agile and SAFe environments to support planning, prioritization, testing and implementation of business and technology changes.

Required Qualifications:

  • BS/BA degree or equivalent relevant experience and 7+ years in trust operations, custody, retirement services, investment operations or institutional financial services.
  • Strong custody knowledge with experience in separately managed accounts, unitization, pricing, reconciliation and operational controls.
  • Experience with digital transformation, AI or low-code tools and the ability to translate ambiguous business needs into practical recommendations.
  • Demonstrated risk awareness and experience with audits, regulatory examinations, vendor oversight and process improvement.
  • Excellent communication, consulting and presentation skills, with the ability to engage clients, prospects, attorneys, senior leaders, auditors, regulators and the Board.
  • Strong influence, organization, analysis, decision-making and issue-resolution skills in a matrix environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with recordkeeping and custody platforms is preferred.
  • Thorough understanding of NSCC offerings.
  • Experience in large scale asset transitions

This includes taking projects from initiation through final implementation, defining ongoing extensions/improvements, driving platform maturity, and closely aligning production support to address any related incidents and issues.

title: Associate Procure to Pay Specialist
description:
At Dow, we believe in putting people first and we’re passionate about delivering integrity, respect and safety to our customers, our employees and the planet.

Our people are at the heart of our solutions. They reflect the communities we live in and the world where we do business. Their diversity is our strength. We’re a community of relentless problem solvers that offers the daily opportunity to contribute with your perspective, transform industries and shape the future. Our purpose is simple - to deliver a sustainable future for the world through science and collaboration. If you’re looking for a challenge and meaningful role, you’re in the right place.

About this role
Dow has an opportunity for an Associate Procure to Pay Specialist within the APAC Procure to Pay organization. In this role, you will support regional process governance, stakeholder engagement, operational issue resolution, and continuous improvement in partnership with experienced team members and business partners.

You will collaborate with Procurement, Sourcing, Integrated Supply Chain, Finance, Diamond Systems Solutions, Source to Pay Solutions, and external service providers to help simplify processes, strengthen controls, improve service delivery, and enhance the employee and supplier experience.

You will apply process knowledge, analytical thinking, and digital capabilities to support practical and sustainable solutions that improve operational efficiency, reduce process waste, and provide useful insights for business decisions.

This role requires working knowledge of Procure to Pay processes and enterprise systems, together with an interest in operational excellence. You will translate business needs into process improvements and digital solutions, work with a moderate level of guidance, and contribute to APAC and global Procurement transformation priorities.


Responsibilities

  • Operational Governance and Service Delivery

Support the APAC regional team in managing Procure to Pay operational escalations and coordinating timely issue resolution.

Work with the Dow Source to Pay (StP) Solutions team in Mumbai and third-party managed service providers (IBM) to support day-to-day operations, issue resolution, service improvements, and knowledge sharing activities.

Monitor service performance, identify recurring issues, and support continuous improvement efforts to enhance service quality and operational efficiency.

Work with Quality Service Managers and operational teams to perform root cause analysis and help implement sustainable corrective actions for recurring issues.

Support development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of PtP process standards, procedures, controls, and documentation.

Assist with stakeholder training, knowledge-sharing activities, and communication programs to improve process understanding and adoption.

Provide operational, reporting, coordination, and administrative support for APAC PtP activities and leadership priorities as needed, including management reporting, process documentation, training coordination, compliance activities, business reviews, and special projects. Continuously identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, digitalize, and automate these activities to improve organizational efficiency and effectiveness.

  • Process Improvement and Transformation

Support and coordinate assigned Procure to Pay continuous improvement initiatives across APAC.

Identify process inefficiencies, control gaps, and automation opportunities throughout the procurement, purchasing, invoice processing, and payment lifecycle.

Contribute to cross-functional projects that simplify processes, improve compliance, reduce process waste, and enhance operational effectiveness.

Support the development of business cases, data analysis, and implementation activities for operational excellence and transformation initiatives.

Measure and communicate project outcomes through KPI tracking, reporting, and value realization metrics.

  • Cross Functional Collaboration

Partner with stakeholders in Procurement, Sourcing, ISC, Finance, DSS, Business IT, Tax, Treasury, and other functions to drive end-to-end process improvements.

Support collaboration between business users, technology teams, and service delivery organizations to help implement practical process and system improvements.

Support implementation of system enhancements, process changes, testing activities, and change management initiatives.

Participate in regional and global transformation programs to ensure APAC requirements and business priorities are represented and achieved.

  • Digitalization Automation and Data Analytics

Support the design, development, testing, and implementation of digital and automation solutions using Power BI, Power Automate, VBA, UiPath, AI enabled tools, and other approved technologies.

Collaborate with DSS, Business IT, and functional stakeholders to identify opportunities for digitalization and process automation.

Develop dashboards, reporting tools, and analytical solutions that provide meaningful operational insights and support data-driven decision making.

Promote adoption of digital tools and innovative ways of working across the APAC PtP organization.

Stay informed of emerging technologies and best practices and share ideas that could improve procurement and finance operations.

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Supply Chain, Information Systems, Engineering, or other relevant disciplines.

3+ years of experience in Procure-to-Pay, Procurement Operations, Finance Operations, Shared Services, or related business processes.

Your skills

Experience utilizing enterprise business systems such as SAP and ServiceNow.

Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder collaboration skills.

Ability to communicate effectively in Business English (written and spoken).

Ability to identify process inefficiencies and contribute to simplification, automation, or digital solutions that reduce manual work and improve productivity.

Experience or demonstrated ability to work effectively with cross-functional stakeholders including Procurement, Sourcing, Finance, Integrated Supply Chain, Information Systems, and Digital organizations.

Additional notes

The following skills are considered highly preferred:

Experience designing and implementing automation solutions using Power BI, Power Automate, UiPath, VBA, AI-enabled tools, or similar technologies.

Experience supporting regional or global process improvement or transformation projects while balancing improvement work with operational responsibilities.

Experience working with shared service centers, managed service providers, or business process outsourcing organizations.

Certification or training in Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, Project Management, Data Analytics, Automation, or Digital Transformation.

Language proficiency in Japanese and/or Korean.

Note: This role does not offer relocation assistance.

Benefits – What Dow offers you

We invest in you.

Dow invests in total rewards programs to help you manage all aspects of you: your pay, your health, your life, your future, and your career. You bring your background, talent, and perspective to work every day. Dow rewards that commitment by investing in your total wellbeing.

Here are just a few highlights of what you would be offered as a Dow employee:

  • Equitable and market-competitive base pay and bonus opportunity across our global markets, along with locally relevant incentives.
  • Benefits and programs to support your physical, mental, financial, and social well-being, to help you get the care you need...when you need it.
  • Competitive retirement program that may include company-provided benefits, savings opportunities, financial planning, and educational resources to help you achieve your long term financial-goals.
    • Employee stock purchase programs (availability varies depending on location).
  • Student Debt Retirement Savings Match Program (U.S. only).
    • Dow will take the value of monthly student debt payments and apply them as if they are contributions to the Employees’ Savings Plan (401(k)), helping employees reach the Company match.
  • Robust medical and life insurance packages that offer a variety of coverage options to meet your individual needs. Travel insurance is also available in certain countries/locations.
  • Opportunities to learn and grow through training and mentoring, work experiences, community involvement and team building.
  • Workplace culture empowering role-based flexibility to maximize personal productivity and balance personal needs.
  • Competitive yearly vacation allowance.
  • Paid time off for new parents (birthing and non-birthing, including adoptive and foster parents).
  • Paid time off to care for family members who are sick or injured.
  • Paid time off to support volunteering and Employee Resource Group’s (ERG) participation.
  • Wellbeing Portal for all Dow employees, our one-stop shop to promote wellbeing, empowering employees to take ownership of their entire wellbeing journey.
  • On-site fitness facilities to help stay healthy and active (availability varies depending on location).
  • Employee discounts for online shopping, cinema tickets, gym memberships and more.
  • Additionally, some of our locations might offer:
    • Transportation allowance (availability varies depending on location)
    • Meal subsidiaries/vouchers (availability varies depending on location)
    • Carbon-neutral transportation incentives e.g. bike to work (availability varies depending on location)

Join our team, we can make a difference together.

About Dow
Dow (NYSE: DOW) is one of the world’s leading materials science companies, serving customers in high-growth markets such as packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer applications. Our global breadth, asset integration and scale, focused innovation, leading business positions and commitment to sustainability enable us to achieve profitable growth and help deliver a sustainable future. We operate manufacturing sites in 30 countries and employ approximately 36,000 people. Dow delivered sales of approximately $43 billion in 2024. References to Dow or the Company mean Dow Inc. and its subsidiaries. ​​​​Learn more about us and our ambition to be the most innovative, customer-centric, inclusive and sustainable materials science company in the world by visiting .

title: Corporate Team Lead - Employee Benefits
description:
Who are we?

Howden is a global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mindset, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 56 countries.

People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It’s what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down headhunters for years. Whatever your priorities – work / life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering – you’ll find like-minded people driving change at Howden.

Based in our Dublin Ringsend office, Howden Ireland are delighted to have a vacancy as a Corporate Team Lead that will be an integral part of our wider Howden Employee Benefits team.


About the Role:

The Corporate Employee Benefits Team Lead will play a key leadership role in the continued growth and development of Howden Ireland's Employee Benefits business.


The successful candidate will lead the development of our Corporate Employee Benefits proposition, managing and growing relationships with key corporate clients while helping to build a dedicated corporate consulting capability over time.


Working closely with the Director of Employee Benefits and the SME Team Lead, this role offers the opportunity to do more than manage an existing portfolio. The successful candidate will help shape the future direction of Corporate Employee Benefits at Howden Ireland, influence strategy, build a dedicated corporate consulting capability and enhance our client proposition and contribute to establishing Howden as a leading Employee Benefits adviser in Ireland.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead the development of the Corporate Employee Benefits segment and contribute to the overall Employee Benefits growth strategy.
  • Work closely with the SME Team Lead to ensure a consistent client experience, effective resource sharing, and alignment of standards across the business.
  • Support the development of colleagues across the wider Employee Benefits team through coaching, mentoring, and technical guidance.
  • Develop and execute plans to support retention, organic growth, cross-selling and new client acquisition.
  • Lead and support presentations, tenders, and new business opportunities.
  • Identify opportunities across Pensions, Health, Risk, Wellbeing and Financial Education services.
  • Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders, referral partners, and external contacts to generate opportunities.
  • Maintain pipeline discipline, forecasting, and commercial oversight.
  • Oversee the delivery of an exceptional client experience across the corporate portfolio.
  • Work closely with the SME Team Lead and wider Employee Benefits leadership team to deliver a consistent client proposition and shared business objectives.
  • Contribute to workforce planning, organisational development, and future team structure.
  • Collaborate across Financial Planning, Commercial Insurance, Personal Lines and Mortgages to support client growth opportunities.
  • Act as a senior adviser and escalation point for key clients.
  • Support clients on benefit strategy, governance, provider selection, employee engagement, and market developments.
  • Ensure high-quality reviews, renewals, and service delivery.
  • Help shape and evolve Howden's Employee Benefits proposition.
  • Work with insurers, providers, marketing, and operational teams to develop new solutions and service enhancements.
  • Monitor market, regulatory and competitor developments and translate these into client insights.
  • Support thought leadership, client communications, seminars, and market engagement activities.

Our success is primarily down to the incredible people we employ.

A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:

title: Mgr, Maintenance
description:
Job descriptions may display in multiple languages based on your language selection.

What we offer:

At Magna, you can expect an engaging and dynamic environment where you can help to develop industry-leading automotive technologies. We invest in our employees, providing them with the support and resources they need to succeed. As a member of our global team, you can expect exciting, varied responsibilities as well as a wide range of development prospects. Because we believe that your career path should be as unique as you are.

Group Summary:

Magna Mechatronics & Mirrors develops intelligent access and vision systems that enhance vehicle safety, functionality, and user interaction. As a global automotive supplier and full-system partner, Magna brings together expertise across Mechatronics and Mirror systems to deliver integrated solutions that support the evolution of vehicle architectures.

Job Responsibilities:

JOB SUMMARY:

Responsible for the planning, supervision/staffing, and implementation of all phases of maintenance. Keeps all production equipment well-maintained and able to meet planning production schedules and goals. Maintains a world class appearance to facilities and grounds. Facilitates the work of departmental personnel by providing leadership and training, enabling them to meet business group, departmental, and personal goals. Is involved in all technical aspects of the design, installation, and operation of manufacturing equipment used in a complex manufacturing facility. Implements and maintains systems within the department that provide efficient operating procedures and data collection for decision making, equipment and project justification and departmental performance measurements.


JOB DUTIES:

1. Machine Maintenance – Manages the maintenance and repair of all production equipment.

a. Maintains all equipment in prime working condition.

b. Ensures all repairs are done in an efficient and professional manner.

c. Sets high quality and workmanship standards for the department and reviews work to assure that it meets or exceeds excepted industrial standards.

d. Determines that all electrical work is in compliance with the requirements of the National Electrical Code, state and local codes and Magna Mirrors practices.

e. Responsible for ensuring all company and business group safety standards and procedures are followed. Takes immediate action to correct any unsafe condition that may arise.

f. Schedules necessary maintenance and repairs so as to least interfere with manufacturing priorities and schedules.

g. Identifies problems with existing equipment and works closely with the facilities equipment group to eliminate them and improve performance and reliability.

h. Reviews preliminary design of all new equipment for potential problems, ease of maintenance, and safety.

i. Implements all major modification to production equipment including installations and relocations.

j. Selects and manages the use of outside contractors to assist in major repairs or projects.

2. Preventative Maintenance—Will establish an effective preventative maintenance system with continuous improvement to achieve total Productive Maintenance implementation.

3. Plant Maintenance – Supervises the maintenance and repair of all buildings and grounds.

a. Responsible for the maintenance of manufacturing and building support systems, i.e., compressed air, process water, H.V.A.C., etc…

b. Maintains corporate buildings and offices as assigned.

c. Supervises janitorial and custodial work in the Newaygo facility.

d. Selects and manages various outside contractors such as custodians, snow removal services, trash removal services, and grounds and landscape maintenance.

e. Implements building security procedures and sees that all company security policies are followed.

4. Material Control – Responsible for the selection, procurement and maintenance of spare parts inventory used to accomplish routine maintenance and emergency repairs. Maintains a production supply area that ensures production needs will be met.

a. Ensures that all critical production and facilities equipment is protected with necessary spare parts.

b. Develops spare parts list, equipment specifications and other miscellaneous documents from information obtained from engineering or various equipment manufacturers.

c. Performs economic analysis on all spare parts inventory to guarantee minimal inventory levels, efficient turnover of materials and the purging of obsolete items.

d. Works with other business groups and corporate to insure minimal duplication of materials and to capitalize on corporate buying efficiencies.

e. Maintains a state of the art inventory control system that ensures minimal operating costs and provides the information necessary to maximize control.

f. Works with purchasing to evaluate various programs such as vendor stocking, quality control improvement, electronic ordering and any other programs that may reduce our costs.

5. Financial Performance – Implements systems to monitor department performance and measure critical indicators such as the downtime, expenses, planned maintenance, etc., and performs routine daily responsibilities efficiently and in a professional manner.

a. Manages a preventive maintenance program that reduces downtime and unplanned maintenance, increases machine reliability and corrects potential problems.

b. Maintains a history of all equipment and analyzes machine performance for areas of improvement.

c. Keeps informed of all pertinent matters relative to business group operations, it’s customers, and the automotive industry in general.

6. Managerial- responsible for developing the skill level of the maintenance team; assures that all team members are trained, directed, and motivated to meet business group and company needs while at a distance from corporate resources. Manages skilled trades and apprentice activities for Newaygo facility. Functions as a member of Newaygo Operations Management Team.

REQUIREMENTS:

1. BS or BA degree in business or engineering. Advanced training or experience in mechanical, electrical, or plant engineering highly desirable.

2. Demonstrated experience and skill in providing technical leadership and direction for facility improvement that involves extensive use of HVAC, gas handling, DI, robotics, and paint systems.

3. Six to eight years experience managing maintenance responsibilities in a large (70 to 100 million sales) manufacturing operation.

4. Demonstrated team development and leadership skills. Experience and demonstrated capability in dealing with a variety of technically challenging manufacturing processes and complex facility support systems.

5. Works with EH&S to eliminate ergonomics and safety hazards associated with machines, tools and chemicals. Ensures safety of outside contractors while in facility and maintains safe work environment.

Awareness, Unity, Empowerment:

At Magna, we believe that a diverse workforce is critical to our success. That’s why we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We hire on the basis of experience and qualifications, and in consideration of job requirements, regardless of, in particular, color, ancestry, religion, gender, origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability or gender identity. Magna takes the privacy of your personal information seriously. We discourage you from sending applications via email or traditional mail to comply with GDPR requirements and your local Data Privacy Law.



AI-Assisted Screening Disclosure

As part of our commitment to a fair, consistent, and efficient recruitment process, we may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in the initial screening of applications submitted through our Workday system. These tools help identify qualifications and experience that align with the role requirements. Please note that AI is used solely to support our recruiters. Final decisions are always made by the hiring manager and the hiring team. Importantly, no applicant data is shared externally through these AI tools. All information remains securely within our systems and is handled in accordance with our privacy and data protection policies.


Under conditions defined by applicable law, you may have the right to request an explanation of how AI is used to support decision-making.

If you have any questions or concerns about this process, feel free to contact our Talent Attraction team.

title: Tıbbi Satış Mümessili – Kardiyometabolik Sağlık, Tekirdağ
description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

Sorumlu Olduğu İller: Edirne, Kırklareli, Tekirdağ, İstanbul Avrupa Yakası


Görev Tanımı

Belirli dönemler içerisinde verilen satış ve pazar payı hedeflerine ulaşmak amacıyla, doktor ziyareti, eczane ziyareti ve ilaç alım ihale bilgilerinin takibini gerçekleştirerek sorumlu olduğu ürünlerin medikal değerinin aktarılması ve satış operasyonları ve pazarlama aktiviteleri hedeflerinin zamanında yerine getirilmesinden sorumlu olacaktır.

  • Yüksek bilgi hakimiyeti ve etik standartlar

Sağlık sistemi, hastalık, ürün portföyü ve tedavi seçenekleri ve ilgili tüm etik kodlar hakkında bilgi sahibi olmak, bu bilgileri aktif kullanabilmek.

Sağlık Mesleği Mensuplarının (SMM) tedavi ihtiyaçlarını belirlemek ve bu ihtiyaçlara çözüm sunabilmek için Lilly çalışanlarını ve kaynaklarını etkin kullanabilmek.

  • Analiz ve planlama

Pazar, bölge ve ürünleri analiz etmek, öncelikleri belirlemek ve bunlara uygun planlar yapmak.

  • Harekete geçme, öğrenme ve paylaşma

Olumlu iş sonuçları elde edebileceği fırsatları değerlendirmek, inisiyatif alarak harekete geçmek, bu eylemlerin sonucunu değerlendirerek öğrenimler sağlamak ve bu öğrenimleri ekiplerle paylaşmak.

description:

  • Responsible to ensure smooth transition of the new product from the Program Manager to the Operations:

involving all aspects of the launch - materials, machinery, manpower, measurement and method.

will follow the Advance Product Quality Planning (APQP) established practice

will have the objective of a flawless launch – no quality or delivery concerns executed at minimum cost

  • Work with engineering staff to obtain drawing approvals from suppliers

title: Associate Manager, Audit Operations & Reporting
description:
Join Manulife’s Audit and Advisory Services Professional Practices team in a high-impact role responsible for executive, Board, and Audit Committee reporting and for strengthening the operating processes that support timely, consistent, and insightful reporting across the Audit function.

The role combines executive reporting, stakeholder coordination, risk insight development, and process improvement. The successful candidate will work directly with senior leaders and risk teams, coordinate inputs across lines of defense, and help bring together information from multiple enterprise sources to produce clear and decision-useful reporting.

Position Responsibilities:

Audit Committee, Board and Executive Reporting

  • Lead the preparation and coordination of Audit Committee, Board, Executive Leadership Team, Audit Leadership Team, and other executive reporting materials.
  • Develop clear, concise, and impactful presentations, briefing notes, speaking notes, and executive summaries.
  • Translate complex audit, risk, issue, and performance information into coherent narratives and actionable insights for senior leadership.
  • Ensure reporting is accurate, consistent, appropriately supported, and aligned across governance forums.
  • Coordinate review, challenge, approval, and production processes with senior stakeholders across the organization.

Risk Insights and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Identify emerging themes, common control weaknesses, and risk insights across audit results to strengthen executive reporting and decision support.
  • Engage directly with executives, governance committees, and internal stakeholders to clarify messages, resolve gaps, and align reporting.

Reporting Operations and Data Coordination

  • Own end-to-end reporting routines, calendars, templates, inputs, quality reviews, action tracking, and delivery milestones.
  • Bring together information from Enterprise GRC and other relevant enterprise sources to support efficient preparation of initial report drafts.
  • Partner with data owners and contributors to improve data quality, reporting consistency, and traceability to source information.
  • Maintain effective controls over version management, review status, approvals, and final reporting packages.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce manual effort, streamline handoffs, and improve the speed and repeatability of report production.

Automation and Continuous Improvement

  • Define business requirements, templates, workflow expectations, and quality criteria for reporting enhancements.
  • Test automation solutions built and improve usability and adoption.
  • Develop guidance and working practices that support consistent, sustainable reporting processes across the Audit function.
  • Coordinate special projects that improve governance, operational effectiveness, and management information.

Required Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience in internal audit, risk management, governance, executive reporting, consulting, financial services, or a related field.
  • Strong experience preparing executive-level materials for senior leadership and Board-level audiences.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex audit and risk information into concise, decision-useful messages.
  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, project management, and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Proven ability to manage high-sensitivity, judgment-intensive work and multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and confidence working directly with senior executives, governance committees, risk teams, and data owners.
  • Advanced proficiency in PowerPoint, Excel, and Microsoft Office applications, with the ability to use generative AI responsibly to improve efficiency.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting Audit Committee, Board, Executive Leadership Team, Audit Leadership Team, or comparable executive governance forums.
  • Knowledge of internal audit methodologies, enterprise risk management frameworks, quality assurance programs, and issue reporting.
  • Experience working with Governance, Risk and Compliance platforms, reporting automation, workflow tools, or data visualization solutions.
  • Understanding of the life insurance, wealth and asset management, or broader financial services industry.
  • Professional designation such as MBA, CPA, CIA, CFA, FRM, or an equivalent credential is an asset.

Key Capabilities

  • Executive reporting and narrative development
  • Audit and enterprise risk insight
  • Operational discipline and project coordination
  • Data synthesis and quality orientation
  • Stakeholder management and influence
  • Continuous improvement and technology enablement

When you join our team:

  • We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
  • We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
  • As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

This position was originally posted to ratified SEIU members from 11/05/26 to 11/13/26. The position is now available to be filled by internal candidates that are not members of the ratified Bargaining Unit or External candidates to Sharp.


What You Will Do
To perform various direct patient care activities and assist with basic and advanced endoscopic procedures in the Endoscopy department under the direct supervision of a Registered Nurse and the attending gastroenterologist. Facilitates patient data management through transcription, order entry, and documentation. Supports best use of resources in management on equipment, supplies, and other department resources.

Required Qualifications

  • H.S. Diploma or Equivalent
  • 2 Years endoscopy lab experience.
  • AHA Basic Life Support for Healthcare Professional (AHA BLS Healthcare) - American Heart Association -REQUIRED


Other Qualification Requirements

  • Completion of GI Technical Specialist (GTS) and Advanced GI Technical Specialist (AGTS) programs within 90 days of hire - required. Program completion to be tracked and maintained by the department.


Essential Functions

  • Equipment Maintenance
    Accurate and efficiently provides high level disinfection of all endoscopes/washers based on SGNA guidelines and established Sharp Policy and Procedure.
    Maintains quality log book documentation for regulatory compliance.
    Performs audits and assists in managing inventory.
    Troubleshoots scope washer and performs chemical changes as required.
    Collaborates with department leadership in Quality Management/reporting of endoscope reprocessing, equipment maintenance, and/or relevant areas of regulatory compliance.
  • General Support
    Completes duties within time frames, maintains equipment and supplies, may assist with ordering supplies; restock rooms; ensures optimal workflow by assisting in transfers of patients as necessary; fosters efficient turnaround of rooms.
    Serves as a departmental resource for areas of endoscope reprocessing and equipment maintenance.
    Collaborates with department Leads/Educators/Materials Specialist to identify ongoing educational opportunities for staff.
    Collaborates with departmental Leadership to maintain equipment and supply costs within fiscal budget.
  • Patient Care
    Accurately and efficiently performs patient care activities under the direct supervision of a registered nurse.
    In addition to documented proficiency in assisting the gastroenterologist during basic endoscopic procedures, assists in advanced procedures including but not limited to: Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatopgraphy (ERCP),colonic and esophageal stent placement, EMR, balloon enteroscopy, and Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS)and Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA) where services are provided.
  • Professional Development
    Under direct supervision of department Lead/Educator/Materials Specialist, actively participates in annual competency training for endoscopy staff by evaluating staff knowledge of endoscope maintenance and cleaning.
    Collaborates with departmental Lead/Educator/Materials Specialist to update or develop new endoscope reprocessing competency modules and/or new equipment in-services, as needed.
    Updates knowledge by participating in educational opportunities and changes to SGNA standards of practice.
  • Specimens
    Under the direct supervision of a registered nurse, correctly collects, labels, and processes all types of tissue specimens obtained in the Endoscopy Department.
    Shows proficiency with equipment used to obtain specimens (i.e. EUS needles, snares, biopsy forceps).
    Teaches correct specimen handling to new Endoscopy Technicians and monitors departmental process for specimen management to ensure regulatory compliance.
    Updates knowledge by participating in educational opportunities and changes to SGNA standards of practice.
